Sin Qaf" without the 'Ayn, and it is also so in the codex of Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, related by at-Tabari. Nafi' narrated from Ibn Abbas: "The Ha" is His forbearance (hilmuhu) [in some copies: hukmuhu, with a kaf], "the Mim" is His glory (majduhu), "the 'Ayn" is His knowledge ('ilmuhu), "the Sin" is His radiance (sana'uhu), and "the Qaf" is His power (qudratuhu), by which Allah swore. From Muhammad ibn Ka'b: Allah swore by His forbearance, His glory, His exaltedness, His radiance and His power, that He will not punish whoever seeks refuge in "there is no god but Allah" sincerely from his heart. Ja'far ibn Muhammad and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The Ha" is from ar-Rahman, "the Mim" from al-Majid, "the 'Ayn" from al-'Alim, "the Sin" from al-Quddus, and "the Qaf" from al-Qahir. Mujahid said: They are the openings of the surahs. Abd Allah ibn Buraydah said: It is the name of the mountain that encircles the world. al-Qushayri mentioned, and the wording is that of ath-Tha'labi, that when this verse was revealed, the sorrow appeared on the face of the Prophet (ﷺ), and it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, what has grieved you?" He said: "I was told of calamities that will befall my nation: swallowing up, casting down, a fire that will gather them, a wind that will hurl them into the sea, and signs following one another, connected with the descent of Isa and the emergence of the Dajjal." And Allah knows best. It is also said: This concerns the Prophet (ﷺ): "The Ha" is his Pool that is approached (al-Hawd al-Mawrud), "the Mim" is his extended dominion (mulkuhu al-mamdud), "the 'Ayn" is his existent might ('izzuhu al-mawjud), "the Sin" is his witnessed radiance (sanahu al-mashhud), "the Qaf" is his standing in the praised station (maqam al-mahmud), and his nearness in honor, from the King, the Worshipped.

Ibn Abbas said: There is no prophet who had a Book except that "Ha Mim. 'Ayn Sin Qaf" was revealed to him, and therefore He said: "Thus does He reveal to you and to those before you." Al-Mahdawi said: It has come in a report that "Ha Mim. 'Ayn Sin Qaf" means "I have revealed to the earlier prophets."

Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn Kathir and Mujahid read "yuha" (with a fatha on the ha) in the passive form, related from Ibn Umar. Then the prepositional phrase is in the nominative position, standing in place of the subject. It is also permissible that the subject of the passive verb be a pronoun, meaning: "The Qur'an contained in this surah is revealed to you," and that the name of Allah be in the nominative by means of an implied verb, the estimate being: "Allah reveals it to you," like the reading of Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr: ﴿Glorified in them morning and evening by men﴾ [An-Nur: 36–37], meaning: "men glorify Him." Sibawayh recited:

"Let Yazid be wept for by a humble one in a dispute, and by a disheveled man whom the calamities have bewildered"

[Note in source: the verse is related in Sibawayh's Kitab as: "Labayk Yazid dari' li-khusumatin / wa-mukhtabit mimma tuti'u al-tawa'ih", attributed by Sibawayh to al-Harith ibn Nuhayk, while the author of Khizanat al-Adab attributes it to Nashal ibn Harri in an elegy for Yazid. See the fifth-and-forties evidence.]

He said: "Labayk Yazid," then specified who should weep for him, so the meaning is: "a humble one weeps for him." It is also permissible that it be a subject with an omitted predicate, as if he said: "Allah reveals it"; or with an implied subject, meaning "the one who reveals is Allah"; or that it be a subject with the predicate "al-'Aziz al-Hakim." The rest of the readers read "yuhi ilayka" with a kasra on the ha and the noun in the nominative as the subject.

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾ has been discussed in more than one place [see vol. 2, p. 69, second edition, and vol. 3, p. 278].

The commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 5:

Allah's words: ﴿The heavens are about to ⦅split apart⦆﴾. The common reading (qira'a, recitation) is with the ta' (تَكادُ). Nafi' and Ibn Thabbat and al-Kisa'i read it with the ya' (يَكادُ). "Yatafattarna" (يَتَفَطَّرْنَ) is read by Nafi' and others with the ya' and the ta', with the ta' (ṭa') doubled. This is the common reading. Abu 'Amr, Abu Bakr, al-Mufaddal and Abu 'Ubayd read "yanfaṭirna" (ينفطرن), from infitar (splitting), like Allah's words: ﴿When the sky splits open﴾ [al-Infitar: 1]. The explanation of this has already passed in surah Maryam. [[See vol. 19, p. 242.]] [[See vol. 11, p. 156.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: "The heavens are about to split apart" means that each one of them is about to split above the one next to it, from the saying of the polytheists: ﴿Allah has taken a son﴾ [al-Baqarah: 116]. [[See vol. 2, p. 85.]] al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: "Yatafattarna" means they are cracking from the greatness and majesty of Allah, above them. It was also said: "above them," meaning above the earths, out of fear of Allah, if they were of those who understand.

Allah's words: ﴿And the angels glorify the praise of their Lord﴾. That is, they declare Him far above what is not permissible to attribute to Him and what does not befit His majesty. It was also said that they are amazed at the audacity of the polytheists, so glorification is mentioned in the place of amazement. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: their glorification is an amazement at what they see of those who expose themselves to the wrath of Allah. Ibn 'Abbas said: their glorification is submission because of what they see of the greatness of Allah. The meaning of "bi-hamdi rabbihim" (with the praise of their Lord) is "by the command of their Lord," as al-Suddi said. "And they ask forgiveness for those on the earth": al-Dahhak said: for those on the earth among the believers, and al-Suddi said the same. Its explanation in surah al-Mu'min is: ﴿And they ask forgiveness for those who believe﴾ [Ghafir: 7]. On this view, the angels here are the bearers of the Throne. It was also said that they are all the angels of the heaven, and this is the apparent meaning of al-Kalbi's view. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: it is abrogated (mansukh) by His words: "and they ask forgiveness for those who believe." Al-Mahdawi said: the correct view is that it is not abrogated (naskh, abrogation), because it is a report, and it is specific to the believers. Abu al-Hasan al-Mawardi reported from al-Kalbi: when the angels saw the two angels who were tested and sent to the earth to judge between people, and who were seduced by the star Venus (al-Zuhra) and fled to Idris, who is the grandfather of Abu Nuh, peace be upon them, and asked him to pray for them, the angels glorified the praise of their Lord and asked forgiveness for the children of Adam. Abu al-Hasan ibn al-Hassar said: Some ignorant people have thought that this verse was revealed because of Harut and Marut, and that it is abrogated by the verse in al-Mu'min. They did not know that the bearers of the Throne are specifically singled out for asking forgiveness for the believers only, and that Allah has other angels who ask forgiveness for those on the earth.

Al-Mawardi: Regarding their asking forgiveness for them there are two views. The first: from sins and wrongdoings, which is the apparent view of Muqatil. The second: that it is a request for provision for them and abundance upon them, said by al-Kalbi. I say: this is more apparent, because "the earth" includes the disbeliever and others, whereas on Muqatil's view the disbeliever is not included. A report has been transmitted on this subject, narrated by Asim al-Ahwal from Abu 'Uthman from Salman, who said: When a servant used to remember Allah in ease, and then adversity befell him, the angels would say: "A known voice from a weak human, who used to remember Allah in ease, and now adversity has befallen him," and so they ask forgiveness for him. But if he did not remember Allah in ease, and then adversity befell him, the angels would say: "A strange voice from a human who did not remember Allah in ease, and now adversity has befallen him," and so they do not ask forgiveness. This indicates that the verse concerns those who remember Allah in ease and in adversity, so it is specific to some of those on the earth among the believers. And Allah knows best. It may be that by asking forgiveness they intend seeking forbearance and pardon, in His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds back the heavens and the earth lest they cease﴾ [Fatir: 41], up to His words: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾. And His words: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing﴾ [al-Ra'd: 6]. The intended meaning is forbearance toward them and not hastening to punish them, so it is general. This was said by al-Zamakhshari.

Mutarrif said: We found the most sincere of Allah's servants toward Allah's servants to be the angels, and we found the most deceitful of Allah's servants toward Allah's servants to be the devils. [[See vol. 15, p. 295.]] ﴿Verily, Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾. Some scholars said: He, the Mighty and Majestic, is awe-inspiring and exalted at the beginning, and gentle and glad-tidings-giving at the end.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: "And those who take protectors besides Him" — meaning, idols that they worship. "Allah is Watchful over them" — i.e., He preserves their deeds in order to recompense them for them. "And you are not over them a guardian" — and this (verse) is abrogated (mansukhah) by the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf).

And in the report (khabar): "The sky has groaned (atta), and it has the right to groan (ta'utt)." That is, it made a sound from the weight of its inhabitants because of their great number. Despite their multitude, they do not cease worshipping Allah, whereas these disbelievers associate partners with Him.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 7:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an﴾. That is: just as We revealed to you and to those before you these meanings, so likewise We revealed to you a Qur'an in Arabic, which We have made clear in the language of the Arabs. It has been said: that is, We sent down to you an Arabic Qur'an in the tongue of your people, just as We sent every messenger in the tongue of his people. The meaning is one and the same. [[In (manuscript) L: there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the wording of this sentence, and it does not depart from the wording or the meaning.]] ﴿That you may warn the Mother of Cities﴾, meaning Makkah. Makkah was called the Mother of Cities because the earth was spread out (duhiyat) from beneath it. ﴿And those around it﴾, from among all of creation. ﴿And warn of the Day of Assembly﴾, that is, by the Day of Assembly, which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿About which there is no doubt﴾, meaning there is no uncertainty in it. ﴿A party will be in the Garden and a party in the Blaze﴾ is a complete sentence in the form of a subject and predicate (mubtada' wa khabar). Al-Kisa'i permitted the accusative (nasb) reading, on the basis of the implied sense: "that you may warn a party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze."

Al-Qurtubi's commentary on Surah 42, verse 8:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made them one community﴾. Al-Dahhak said: a people of one religion, either people of misguidance or people of guidance. "But He admits whom He wills into His mercy." Anas ibn Malik said: into Islam. "And the wrongdoers" is in the nominative because it is the subject (mubtada', the inchoative), and the predicate is "for them there is no protector nor helper," which is coordinated upon the wording (ma'tuf 'ala al-lafz), so "wa-la nasir" is in the genitive. It is also permissible to read "wa-la nasirin" in the nominative, coordinated upon the position (al-mawdi'), with "min" being redundant (za'idah).

"Or have they taken" means "rather, they have taken." "Protectors (awliya') besides Him" means idols. "Then God is the Protector" means: your Protector, O Muhammad, and the Protector of whoever follows you, with no protector besides Him. [[What is between the brackets is from manuscripts ح ل هـ.]] "And He gives life to the dead" means at the Resurrection. "And He is capable of all things" and others among the protectors have no power over anything.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 10:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whatever you differ about, its ruling is with Allah﴾. This is a report of the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the believers, meaning: and whatever the disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists oppose you in, regarding matters of the religion, then say to them: its judgment belongs to Allah, not to you. He has decided that the religion is Islam and nothing other than it. And matters of the sacred laws (shara'i') are only to be received (yatalaqqa) from the explanation (bayan) of Allah. ﴿That is Allah, my Lord﴾: meaning, the One described by these attributes is my Lord alone. Within this there is an implied element (idmar): that is, say to them, O Muhammad: "That is Allah, who gives life to the dead and judges between those who differ, is my Lord." ﴿In Him I have put my trust﴾: I have relied upon (i'tamadtu). ﴿And to Him I turn back﴾: I return (arji').

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 11:

﴿He has made for you mates from among yourselves, and of the cattle, mates; He multiplies you thereby. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾ (42:11)

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾. It is read with a nominative ending (raf') as an adjectival qualifier (na't) of the name of Allah, or as an implied "He is the Originator" (taqdir: huwa fatiruh). It is also permissible to read it in the accusative (nasb) as a vocative (nida'), and in the genitive (jarr) as an apposition (badal) to the pronoun in "'alayhi" (upon Him).

Al-Fatir (the Originator) means al-Mubdi' (the One who innovates and creates without precedent) and al-Khaliq (the Creator). This has already been discussed (see vol. 6 p. 397, vol. 9 pp. 270 and 346, vol. 14 pp. 24 ff., 319).

"He made for you mates from among yourselves" – it is said its meaning is females. He said "from among yourselves" because He created Hawwa' (Eve) from the rib of Adam. Mujahid said: offspring after offspring.

"And of the cattle, mates" – meaning the eight kinds mentioned in "al-An'am" (see vol. 7 p. 113, first or second edition): the males and females of camels, cattle, sheep and goats.

"He multiplies you thereby" – that is, He creates you and brings you into being "thereby," i.e., in the womb (al-rahm). It is also said: in the belly (al-batn).

Al-Farra' and Ibn Kaysan said: "thereby" (fihi) means "by it" (bihi). Likewise al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "yadhra'ukum fihi" is "yukaththirukum bihi," i.e., He multiplies you by it, by making you mates (azwaj), that is, spouses (halail), because they are the cause of offspring.

It is also said: the pronoun in "fihi" refers to the act of making (al-ja'l), which is indicated by "ja'ala," so it is as if He said: He creates you and multiplies you through the making.

Ibn Qutaybah: "yadhra'ukum fihi" means "in the mate," i.e., He creates you in the bellies of females. He said: "fihi" may refer to the womb, but this is far-fetched, because the womb is feminine and no prior mention of it has preceded.

"There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing." It is said: the particle "ka" (like) is extra (za'idah) for emphasis, meaning "laysa mithlahu shay'" (there is nothing like Him). The poet said:

*"And hearth-stones like those upon which the pots are set (yu'tha-faynа)"*

[Note: al-salyat are the three stones upon which the cooking pot is placed; yu'thafin means they are set up to hold the pot. See Khizanat al-Adab, the fifth shahid after the 135th, and Sibawayh's book.]

So he introduced a second "ka" upon the first "ka" as an emphasis of the comparison. It is also said: "mithl" is extra for emphasis, and this is the view of Tha'lab: "laysa kahuwa shay'," like the verse: ﴿If they believe in the like of what you believed in, then they are rightly guided﴾ (2:137). In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "If they believe in what you believed in, then they are rightly guided." Aws ibn Hajar said:

*"And slain men like the trunks of palm trees, over whom pours a steady rain"*

That is, "like the trunks" (ka-juthu').

What one must believe in this matter is that Allah, may His name be exalted, in His greatness, His majesty, His dominion, the excellence of His names and the loftiness of His attributes, resembles none of His creatures and is not likened to any of them. What has come in the Shari'ah applying to the Creator and the created is used in a figurative sense, so there is no resemblance between them in the real meaning, since the attributes of the Eternal, exalted is He, are unlike the attributes of the created, for their attributes do not cease to be tied to accidents and qualities, whereas He, exalted is He, is far removed from that. Rather He has always been with His names and attributes, as we have explained in (al-Kitab al-Asna fi Sharh Asma' Allah al-Husna). And the saying of the Truth suffices in this: "There is nothing like unto Him." Some of the verifying scholars have said: Tawhid is affirming an Essence that does not resemble essences, and is not devoid of attributes. Al-Wasiti, may Allah have mercy on him, added further clarification, saying: There is no essence like His Essence, no name like His name, no act like His act, and no attribute like His attribute, except in terms of agreement in wording. The Eternal Essence is too exalted to have a newly-arisen attribute, just as it is impossible for a created essence to have an eternal attribute. All of this is the doctrine of the People of the Truth, the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Haqq wa al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah). May Allah be pleased with them!

The saying of Allah Most High: ﴿To Him belong the keys (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth﴾. Its explanation has already passed in "az-Zumar" [[See vol. 15, p. 274.]]. An-Nahhas said: Whoever possesses the keys possesses the treasuries. The key is called iqlid (key), and its plural is formed irregularly, like mahasin, while the singular is husn.

﴿He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it. Indeed, He is All-Knowing of everything﴾ has already passed in several places [[See vol. 1, p. 621 (second or third edition), and vol. 9, p. 314.]].

**The Qur'anic verse (42:13–14) and the commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an)**

**Allah's saying: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah﴾.** There are two issues here.

**The first issue: Allah's saying ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion﴾.** That is, He who holds the keys of the heavens and the earth has prescribed for you of the religion what He prescribed for the people of Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus. Then He explained this in His saying: **"That you establish the religion"**, which is the Oneness of Allah, obedience to Him, belief in His messengers and His books, belief in the Day of Recompense, and all that by establishing which a person becomes a Muslim. He did not mean the *shari'ah* (sacred law, the detailed rules), which are the interests of the nations according to their circumstances, for these differ and vary. Allah said: ﴿For each of you We have appointed a law and a method﴾ (5:48). This matter has already been discussed [see vol. 6, p. 211 of this edition].

The word *shara'a* means: he laid down a path, made clear and explained the ways. It is said: *shara'a lahum yashra'u shar'an*, meaning he legislated (*sanna*) [in one copy: "i.e., he explained"]. *Al-shari'* is the broadest road. A dwelling is said to be *shurii'a* when it is on a open, passable road. *Shara'tu al-ibil* means I let the camels reach the watering place (*al-shari'ah*). *Shara'tu al-adim* means I flayed the hide. Ya'qub said: when you split what is between the two legs (of an animal, to flay it). He said: I heard this from Umm al-Harmasis al-Bakriyya. *Shara'tu fi hadha al-amr shuruu'an* means I plunged into this matter.

**"That you establish the religion"**: the *'an* here (*"an"*, "that") is in the nominative position (*mahall raf'*), on the assumption that the meaning is: "And that which He enjoined upon Noah is that you establish the religion." On this reading one stops at *'Isa* (Jesus). It has also been said that it is in the accusative, meaning: He prescribed for you the establishment of the religion. It has also been said that it is in the genitive, substituted for the *ha'* in *bihi* (in "with which"), as if He said: "with it, establish the religion." On these two readings one does not stop at *'Isa*. It is also permissible that *"an"* is explanatory (*mufassira*), like ﴿*an imshu*﴾ ("walk", 38:6), in which case it has no place in the grammatical structure (*i'rab*, the grammatical analysis of word endings).

**The second issue:** The judge Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi said: It is established in the authentic hadith that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, in the great and well-known hadith of intercession: *"But go to Noah, for he is the first messenger whom Allah sent to the people of the earth; so they will come to Noah and say to him: 'You are the first messenger whom Allah sent to the people of the earth...'"*

[This is sound and there is no difficulty in it, just as Adam is the first prophet without difficulty, because Adam had with him only prophethood, and obligatory duties were not imposed on him, nor were the forbidden things legislated for him. He was only given guidance regarding some matters, and confined to the necessities of livelihood, and to the duties of life and survival. Then the period extended until Noah, and Allah sent him with the prohibition of mothers, daughters and sisters, and imposed on him the obligations, and clarified for him the good manners in religious matters. This continued to be strengthened through the messengers, who support one another (the text has "yatanasar" in one version, "yatanashar" in another), through the prophets, may the blessings of Allah be upon them, one after another, and law following law, until Allah sealed them with the best of religions, our religion, through the tongue of the most noble of messengers, our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). So the meaning is: "We have enjoined on you, O Muhammad, and on Noah, one religion," meaning in the fundamentals on which the sacred law does not differ: the Oneness of God, prayer, zakat, fasting, pilgrimage, drawing near to Allah through righteous deeds, seeking nearness to Him through what turns the heart and the limbs towards Him, truthfulness, fulfilling covenants, returning trusts, maintaining ties of kinship, forbidding disbelief, killing, adultery and harming creation in any way, transgressing against animals wherever they are, and committing base acts or what destroys manliness. All this was legislated as one religion and one united community, not differing on the tongues of the prophets, even though their numbers differed. This is His saying: ﴿*That you establish the religion and do not be divided therein*﴾ (42:13), meaning: make it standing, meaning lasting, continuous, preserved and firm, without disagreement or instability in it. Among the creatures there are those who fulfilled it, and among them are those who broke it, and whoever breaks it, breaks it only against himself (cf. 48:10) [see p. 286 of this part]. The sacred laws differed after this in certain aspects, according to what Allah willed, in matters which the interest required and wisdom made necessary to establish for the nations in their times.] And Allah knows best.

Mujahid said: Allah never sent a prophet but He enjoined on him the establishment of prayer, the giving of zakat, and acknowledgment of obedience to Allah. That is the religion He prescribed for them. This is also the statement of al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas, and it is the view of al-Kalbi. Qatada said: it means the permitting of what is lawful and the forbidding of what is unlawful. Al-Hakam said: it means the prohibition of mothers, sisters and daughters. What the judge mentioned includes these statements and adds to them. He singled out Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus for mention because they are the masters of the sacred laws.

**Allah's saying: ﴿It is hard for the polytheists﴾**, that is, it is great and grievous for them, **"what you call them to"**, namely the Oneness of God and the rejection of idols. Qatada said: It was hard for the polytheists, so the testimony that there is no god but Allah was grievous to them, and Iblis and his armies were distressed by it, but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, refused except to help it, to make it exalted, and to make it prevail over those who opposed it. Then He said: **"Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills"**, that is, He selects. *Al-ijtiba'* means selection, that is, He selects for the Oneness whom He wills. **"And guides to Himself whoever turns back"**, that is, He purifies for His religion whoever returns to Him.

**"And they did not divide"**. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means the Quraysh. **"Except after knowledge had come to them"**, that is Muhammad (ﷺ). They used to wish that a prophet would be sent to them. The evidence is the saying of Allah in Surah Fatir: ﴿*They swore by Allah with their most solemn oaths that if a warner came to them*﴾ (35:42) [see vol. 14, p. 357], meaning a prophet. He also said in Surah al-Baqara: ﴿*When there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it*﴾ (2:89), as its explanation was given there [see vol. 2, p. 27]. It has also been said: it means the nations of the earlier prophets, for among them there was disagreement after the period was prolonged, so some people believed and some disbelieved. Ibn 'Abbas also said: it means the People of the Book. The evidence is in Surah al-Bayyina: ﴿*Those who were given the Book did not divide except after the clear proof came to them*﴾ (98:4) [see vol. 17, p. 146]. So the polytheists said: why was he singled out for prophethood? The Jews envied him when he was sent, and likewise the Christians. **"Out of envy among themselves"**, that is, envy of some of them towards others, seeking leadership. Their division was not due to a deficiency in the clarity of the evidence and the proofs, but to envy, injustice and preoccupation with worldly affairs.

**"And had it not been for a word that had preceded from your Lord"** [see vol. 20, p. 143] **"concerning the delay of punishment from these people"**, **"until an appointed term,"** it has been said: the Resurrection, because of His saying: ﴿*Nay, the Hour is their appointed time*﴾ (54:46). It has also been said: until the term at which their punishment was decreed. **"Then the matter would have been decided between them"**, that is, between those who believed and those who disbelieved, by the descent of punishment. **"And indeed those who were given the Book after them"** means the Jews and the Christians. **"After them"**, that is, after those who differed about the truth. **"Are in doubt"** about that which the prophets enjoined. "The Book" here means the Torah and the Gospel. It has also been said: **"Those who were given the Book"** are the Quraysh, **"after them"** means after the Jews and Christians, **"are in doubt"** about the Qur'an or about Muhammad. Mujahid said: the meaning of **"after them"** is "before them", that is, before the polytheists of Mecca, and they are the Jews and the Christians.

**The Qur'anic verse (42:13–14) and the commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an)**

**Allah's saying: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah﴾.** There are two issues here.

**The first issue: Allah's saying ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion﴾.** That is, He who holds the keys of the heavens and the earth has prescribed for you of the religion what He prescribed for the people of Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus. Then He explained this in His saying: **"That you establish the religion"**, which is the Oneness of Allah, obedience to Him, belief in His messengers and His books, belief in the Day of Recompense, and all that by establishing which a person becomes a Muslim. He did not mean the *shari'ah* (sacred law, the detailed rules), which are the interests of the nations according to their circumstances, for these differ and vary. Allah said: ﴿For each of you We have appointed a law and a method﴾ (5:48). This matter has already been discussed [see vol. 6, p. 211 of this edition].

The word *shara'a* means: he laid down a path, made clear and explained the ways. It is said: *shara'a lahum yashra'u shar'an*, meaning he legislated (*sanna*) [in one copy: "i.e., he explained"]. *Al-shari'* is the broadest road. A dwelling is said to be *shurii'a* when it is on a open, passable road. *Shara'tu al-ibil* means I let the camels reach the watering place (*al-shari'ah*). *Shara'tu al-adim* means I flayed the hide. Ya'qub said: when you split what is between the two legs (of an animal, to flay it). He said: I heard this from Umm al-Harmasis al-Bakriyya. *Shara'tu fi hadha al-amr shuruu'an* means I plunged into this matter.

**"That you establish the religion"**: the *'an* here (*"an"*, "that") is in the nominative position (*mahall raf'*), on the assumption that the meaning is: "And that which He enjoined upon Noah is that you establish the religion." On this reading one stops at *'Isa* (Jesus). It has also been said that it is in the accusative, meaning: He prescribed for you the establishment of the religion. It has also been said that it is in the genitive, substituted for the *ha'* in *bihi* (in "with which"), as if He said: "with it, establish the religion." On these two readings one does not stop at *'Isa*. It is also permissible that *"an"* is explanatory (*mufassira*), like ﴿*an imshu*﴾ ("walk", 38:6), in which case it has no place in the grammatical structure (*i'rab*, the grammatical analysis of word endings).

**The second issue:** The judge Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi said: It is established in the authentic hadith that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, in the great and well-known hadith of intercession: *"But go to Noah, for he is the first messenger whom Allah sent to the people of the earth; so they will come to Noah and say to him: 'You are the first messenger whom Allah sent to the people of the earth...'"*

[This is sound and there is no difficulty in it, just as Adam is the first prophet without difficulty, because Adam had with him only prophethood, and obligatory duties were not imposed on him, nor were the forbidden things legislated for him. He was only given guidance regarding some matters, and confined to the necessities of livelihood, and to the duties of life and survival. Then the period extended until Noah, and Allah sent him with the prohibition of mothers, daughters and sisters, and imposed on him the obligations, and clarified for him the good manners in religious matters. This continued to be strengthened through the messengers, who support one another (the text has "yatanasar" in one version, "yatanashar" in another), through the prophets, may the blessings of Allah be upon them, one after another, and law following law, until Allah sealed them with the best of religions, our religion, through the tongue of the most noble of messengers, our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). So the meaning is: "We have enjoined on you, O Muhammad, and on Noah, one religion," meaning in the fundamentals on which the sacred law does not differ: the Oneness of God, prayer, zakat, fasting, pilgrimage, drawing near to Allah through righteous deeds, seeking nearness to Him through what turns the heart and the limbs towards Him, truthfulness, fulfilling covenants, returning trusts, maintaining ties of kinship, forbidding disbelief, killing, adultery and harming creation in any way, transgressing against animals wherever they are, and committing base acts or what destroys manliness. All this was legislated as one religion and one united community, not differing on the tongues of the prophets, even though their numbers differed. This is His saying: ﴿*That you establish the religion and do not be divided therein*﴾ (42:13), meaning: make it standing, meaning lasting, continuous, preserved and firm, without disagreement or instability in it. Among the creatures there are those who fulfilled it, and among them are those who broke it, and whoever breaks it, breaks it only against himself (cf. 48:10) [see p. 286 of this part]. The sacred laws differed after this in certain aspects, according to what Allah willed, in matters which the interest required and wisdom made necessary to establish for the nations in their times.] And Allah knows best.

Mujahid said: Allah never sent a prophet but He enjoined on him the establishment of prayer, the giving of zakat, and acknowledgment of obedience to Allah. That is the religion He prescribed for them. This is also the statement of al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas, and it is the view of al-Kalbi. Qatada said: it means the permitting of what is lawful and the forbidding of what is unlawful. Al-Hakam said: it means the prohibition of mothers, sisters and daughters. What the judge mentioned includes these statements and adds to them. He singled out Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus for mention because they are the masters of the sacred laws.

**Allah's saying: ﴿It is hard for the polytheists﴾**, that is, it is great and grievous for them, **"what you call them to"**, namely the Oneness of God and the rejection of idols. Qatada said: It was hard for the polytheists, so the testimony that there is no god but Allah was grievous to them, and Iblis and his armies were distressed by it, but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, refused except to help it, to make it exalted, and to make it prevail over those who opposed it. Then He said: **"Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills"**, that is, He selects. *Al-ijtiba'* means selection, that is, He selects for the Oneness whom He wills. **"And guides to Himself whoever turns back"**, that is, He purifies for His religion whoever returns to Him.

**"And they did not divide"**. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means the Quraysh. **"Except after knowledge had come to them"**, that is Muhammad (ﷺ). They used to wish that a prophet would be sent to them. The evidence is the saying of Allah in Surah Fatir: ﴿*They swore by Allah with their most solemn oaths that if a warner came to them*﴾ (35:42) [see vol. 14, p. 357], meaning a prophet. He also said in Surah al-Baqara: ﴿*When there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it*﴾ (2:89), as its explanation was given there [see vol. 2, p. 27]. It has also been said: it means the nations of the earlier prophets, for among them there was disagreement after the period was prolonged, so some people believed and some disbelieved. Ibn 'Abbas also said: it means the People of the Book. The evidence is in Surah al-Bayyina: ﴿*Those who were given the Book did not divide except after the clear proof came to them*﴾ (98:4) [see vol. 17, p. 146]. So the polytheists said: why was he singled out for prophethood? The Jews envied him when he was sent, and likewise the Christians. **"Out of envy among themselves"**, that is, envy of some of them towards others, seeking leadership. Their division was not due to a deficiency in the clarity of the evidence and the proofs, but to envy, injustice and preoccupation with worldly affairs.

**"And had it not been for a word that had preceded from your Lord"** [see vol. 20, p. 143] **"concerning the delay of punishment from these people"**, **"until an appointed term,"** it has been said: the Resurrection, because of His saying: ﴿*Nay, the Hour is their appointed time*﴾ (54:46). It has also been said: until the term at which their punishment was decreed. **"Then the matter would have been decided between them"**, that is, between those who believed and those who disbelieved, by the descent of punishment. **"And indeed those who were given the Book after them"** means the Jews and the Christians. **"After them"**, that is, after those who differed about the truth. **"Are in doubt"** about that which the prophets enjoined. "The Book" here means the Torah and the Gospel. It has also been said: **"Those who were given the Book"** are the Quraysh, **"after them"** means after the Jews and Christians, **"are in doubt"** about the Qur'an or about Muhammad. Mujahid said: the meaning of **"after them"** is "before them", that is, before the polytheists of Mecca, and they are the Jews and the Christians.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 15:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So to that [faith] invite, and remain steadfast as you have been commanded﴾. When it was permitted that the doubt [mentioned earlier] belongs to the Jews and the Christians, or to the Quraysh, it was said to him: "So to that invite," meaning: since you have clarified their doubt, invite [them] to God, that is, to that religion which God prescribed for the prophets and enjoined upon them. Thus the lam (al-lam, the particle "li") is in the sense of ila ("to"), as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired her﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 5], meaning "to her." And "dhalika" (that) is in the sense of "hadha" (this). This has already been discussed at the beginning of al-Baqarah [see vol. 1, p. 157, second or third edition]. The meaning is: "So for this Quran, invite." It has also been said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the sentence, and the meaning is: what you call them to is heavy upon the polytheists, so invite [them] to it. It has also been said: the lam is in its original function, and the meaning is: "Because of that which was mentioned before, invite and remain steadfast." Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, to the Quran, so invite the creation. "And remain steadfast" is an address to him, peace be upon him. Qatadah said: that is, remain steadfast upon the command of God. Sufyan said: that is, remain steadfast upon the Quran. Al-Dahhak said: remain steadfast in conveying the message. "And do not follow their desires" means: do not look to the opposition of those who oppose you. "And say: I believe in whatever Book God has sent down, and I am commanded to act justly among you" means: that I act justly, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Ghafir: 66]. It has also been said: it is the lam of purpose (lam kay), meaning: so that I may act justly. Ibn 'Abbas and Abu al-'Aliyah said: so that I may make equal among you in religion, so that I believe in every Book and every Messenger. Others said: so that I act justly in all circumstances. It has also been said: this justice is justice in the rulings, and it has been said: it is justice in conveying [the message]. "God is our Lord and your Lord; for us are our deeds and for you are your deeds; there is no argument between us and you" — Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: the address is to the Jews, meaning: for us is our religion and for you is your religion. He said: then it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day﴾ [al-Tawbah: 29], the verse. Mujahid said: the meaning of "there is no argument between us and you" is: there is no dispute between us and you. It has also been said: it is not abrogated, because the proofs have become manifest and the evidences have been established, so nothing remains but obstinacy, and after obstinacy there is no argument and no disputation. Al-Nahhas said: it is also possible that, according to that view, the meaning of "there is no argument between us and you" is: he was not commanded to argue against you and to fight you; then this was abrogated. Just as if someone had said, before the qibla was changed: "Do not pray toward the Ka'bah," and then people were afterward turned, it would be correct to say that this was abrogated. "God will gather us together" — he means the Day of Resurrection. "And to Him is the final return" means: He will judge between us when we come to Him, and will recompense each according to what he was upon. It has also been said: this verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, who asked the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, to turn back from his call and his religion to the religion of Quraysh, on condition that al-Walid give him half of his wealth and Shaybah marry him to his daughter.

The words of the Most High: ﴿Those who argue about God﴾ refers back to the polytheists. "After it has been answered" (*min ba'di ma istujība lahu*). Mujahid said: "After the people have embraced Islam." He said: "These people imagined that the Jahiliyyah would return."

Qatadah said: "Those who argue about God are the Jews and the Christians. Their argument is their saying: 'Our prophet came before your prophet, and our book came before your book.' They regarded themselves as superior because they were People of the Book and because they were the descendants of the prophets." The polytheists used to say: ﴿Which of the two groups is better in station and finer in assembly?﴾ [Maryam: 73].[[See vol. 11, p. 142.]]

Then God the Most High said: "Those who argue about God, after it has been answered, their argument is baseless (*dāḥiḍatun*) with their Lord." That is, it has no stability, like a thing that slips from its place.

The pronoun in *lahu* (in "after it has been answered for Him") may refer to God, mighty and majestic, meaning: after they had affirmed the oneness of God and borne witness to His unity. It may also refer to the Prophet ﷺ, meaning: after his call (to Muhammad ﷺ) had been answered by the people of Badr, and God had given victory to the believers.

It is said: *daḥaḍat ḥujjatuhu duḥūḍan*, meaning "his argument became void." And God *adḥaḍahā*, meaning He nullified it. *Al-idḥāḍ* means causing to slip. A place may be *daḥaḍ* or *daḍḥ* (with vowelling), meaning slippery. *Daḥaḍat rijluhu* (his foot slipped) means it became slippery. And *daḥaḍat al-shamsu 'an kabdi al-samā'* means the sun declined from the middle of the sky.

"And upon them is wrath": he means in this world. "And for them is a severe punishment": he means in the Hereafter, a lasting punishment.

Allah's saying: ﴿It is Allah who has sent down the Book⁠﴾, meaning the Qur'an and the other revealed Books. "with the truth" means with what is true. "and the Balance" means justice; this is what Ibn 'Abbas and most of the exegetes said. Justice is called a balance (mizan), because the balance is the instrument of equity and justice. It has also been said: the Balance is what is made clear in the Books of what a person must act upon. Qatadah said: the Balance is justice in what He commanded and what He forbade. These statements are close in meaning. It has also been said: it is the recompense for obedience with reward and for disobedience with punishment. It has also been said: it is the actual balance with which things are weighed. He sent it down from the sky and taught the servants to weigh by it, so that there would be no oppression and cheating among them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Book and the Balance so that people may uphold justice⁠﴾ [[Verse 25, Surah al-Hadid.]] [al-Hadid: 25]. Mujahid said: it is that by which things are weighed. The meaning of "sent down the Balance" is His inspiring it to creatures so that they may establish it and act by it. It has also been said: the Balance is Muhammad (ﷺ), who judges among you by the Book of Allah.

"And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near" — so He did not inform him of it. This urges him to act upon the Book, justice, and equity, and to act upon the laws before there suddenly comes the Day on which there is accountability and the weighing of deeds, when whoever fulfilled will be repaid in full and whoever cheated will be cheated. So "perhaps the Hour is near" means near to you, while you do not know it. He said "near" (qarib) and did not say "near" in the feminine (qariba), because its feminine form is not real (haqiqi), as it is like a time; this was said by al-Zajjaj. The meaning is: perhaps the Resurrection, or perhaps the coming of the Hour, is near. Al-Kisa'i said: "qarib" is an adjective that is used for the masculine, the feminine and the plural, with one meaning and one form. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good⁠﴾ [[Verse 56, Surah al-A'raf. See vol. 7, p. 227.]] [al-A'raf: 56]. The poet said:

وَكُنَّا قَرِيبًا وَالدِّيَارُ بَعِيدَةً ... فَلَمَّا وصلنا نصب أعينهم غبنا

"We were near while the homes were far; then when we reached them, they kept us before their eyes, and we were absent."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 18:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾. He means: in a manner of mockery, supposing that it will not come, or deceiving the weak [among them] into thinking that it will not happen. "And those who believe are apprehensive of it" – that is, fearful and anxious, because they regard their own selves as falling short despite their striving in obedience, as He said: ﴿And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful, because they are returning to their Lord﴾ [[Verse 60, Surah al-Mu'minun.]] [al-Mu'minun: 60]. "And they know that it is the truth" – that is, the one about which there is no doubt. "Indeed, those who dispute concerning the Hour" – that is, who doubt and argue about the establishment of the Hour – ﴿are in far-reaching error﴾, that is, far from the truth and from the path of reflection, for if they had remembered they would have known that He who created them from dust, then from a drop of semen, until they reached what they reached, is capable of resurrecting them.

The Qur'anic phrase ﴿Allah is Gentle with His servants﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: Knowing of them (ḥafiyy). 'Ikrimah said: Kind to them (bārr). al-Suddi said: Compassionate toward them (rafīq). Muqatil said: He is Gentle toward the righteous and the wicked, in that He does not destroy them with hunger because of their disobediences. al-Qurazi said: He is Gentle with them in the gathering (al-ʿarḍ) and the reckoning (al-muḥāsaba). He said:

Tomorrow, before the Master of creation, the creation will have a standing,
where the Majestic questions them, and is gentle (yalṭufu).

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said: He is gentle with them regarding provision in two respects. First, He made your provision from the good things. Second, He did not give it to you all at once, so that you would squander it.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: He is gentle with them in the Qur'an, its elaboration (tafṣīl) and its explanation (tafsīr).

al-Junayd said: He is gentle with His friends until they know Him, and if He were gentle with His enemies they would not deny Him.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Kattani said: The Gentle One is gentle with whoever of His servants turns to Him for refuge. When he despairs of the creation, he relies on Him and returns to Him, and then He accepts him and turns toward him.

A ḥadīth of the Prophet (ﷺ) has come: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, looks upon the forgotten graves and says, 'Their traces have been effaced, their forms have dissolved, and the punishment remains upon them. I am the Gentle, and I am the Most Merciful of the merciful. Lighten the punishment for them.' So the punishment is lightened for them."

Abu 'Ali al-Thaqafi, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

I pass by the remnants of graves as though I were
a man of insight, while reward in it is scant.
Whoever Allah splits open (his grave), He measures his provision,
and my Lord is Gentle with whoever turns to Him.

It was also said: al-Latif is the One who spreads out the virtues of His servants and conceals their faults from them. On this basis the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O You who manifest the beautiful and conceal the ugly."

It was said: He is the One who accepts the little and gives the abundant.

It was said: He is the One who mends the broken and eases the difficult.

It was said: He is the One whose justice alone is feared and whose grace alone is hoped for.

It was said: He is the One who gives His servant blessing beyond his aspiration and imposes obedience beyond his capacity. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if you count the favor of Allah, you cannot enumerate it﴾ [Ibrahim: 34] [an-Nahl: 18], ﴿And He has amply bestowed upon you His favors, outward and hidden﴾ [Luqman: 20], and He said: ﴿He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ [al-Hajj: 78], ﴿Allah wants to lighten [the burden] for you﴾ [an-Nisa': 28].

It was said: He is the One who helps in service and multiplies praise.

It was said: He is the One who does not hasten to punish those who disobey Him and does not disappoint those who hope in Him.

It was said: He is the One who does not turn away His petitioner and does not make hopeless the one who aspires to Him.

It was said: He is the One who pardons whoever slips.

It was said: He is the One who shows mercy to whoever does not show mercy to himself.

It was said: He is the One who kindled in the secrets of the knowers (al-ʿārifīn), through contemplative witnessing (al-mushāhada), a lamp, made the straight path a clear way for them, and poured out for them from the clouds of His kindness abundant, pouring water.

The statement of Abu al-'Aliyah and also al-Junayd has already passed in *al-An'am* [see vol. 7, p. 57, first or second edition]. We have mentioned all of this in *al-Kitab al-Asna fi Sharh Asma' Allah al-Husna* (The Most Excellent Book on Explaining the Beautiful Names of Allah), under His name al-Latif, and praise be to Allah.

﴿He gives provision to whom He wills﴾, and withholds from whom He wills. In the preference of some people over others in wealth there is wisdom, so that some may take others in service, as He said: ﴿That some of them may take others as subjects﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 32]. Thus this is a kindness toward the servants. Also, so that He may test the wealthy by the poor and the poor by the wealthy, as He said: ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others; will you be patient?﴾ [al-Furqan: 20], as its explanation has already preceded [al-Furqan: 20, see vol. 13, p. 18].

﴿And He is the Strong, the Mighty﴾

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 20:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his tilth﴾. Al-harth (tilth, cultivation) is action and earning. From this is the saying of Abdullah ibn Umar: "Cultivate for your worldly life as if you will live forever, and work for your Hereafter as if you will die tomorrow." From this root a man is named Harith (cultivator). The meaning: whoever seeks, with what We have provided him, a tilth for his Hereafter, by discharging the rights of God and spending for the strengthening of the religion, We will give him the reward of that, multiplied from ten up to seven hundredfold or more. ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world﴾, that is, seeks with the wealth God has given him worldly leadership and the means to forbidden things, We do not deprive him of provision at all, but he has no share in the Hereafter from his wealth. God Exalted says: ﴿Whoever desires the hastening [life], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We desire. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will enter, blamed and banished. And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its due striving while he is a believer, those are the ones whose striving is appreciated﴾ [[Verse 18 onward of Surat al-Isra'.]] [al-Isra': 18–19]. It has been said: ﴿We will increase him in his tilth﴾ means We enable him for worship and make it easy for him. It has been said: the tilth of the Hereafter is obedience, meaning whoever obeys, for him is the reward. It has been said: ﴿We will increase him in his tilth﴾ means We give him the world together with the Hereafter. It has been said: the verse concerns warfare, meaning whoever intends by his fighting the Hereafter is given reward, and whoever intends by his fighting booty is given from it. Al-Qushayri said: The apparent meaning is that the verse concerns the disbeliever, who is granted expansion in this world; that is, he should not be deceived by this, because the world does not last. Qatadah said: God gives, for the intention of the Hereafter, whatever He wills of the affairs of this world, and He does not give, for the intention of this world, except this world. He also said: God says: "Whoever works for his Hereafter, We increase him in his work and give him from the world what We have written for him; and whoever prefers his worldly life over his Hereafter, We will not assign him a share in the Hereafter except the Fire, and he will not attain from this world except a provision We have already apportioned to him, which he will be given whether with preference or without preference." Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas, who said: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter﴾, whoever is among the righteous who desires by his good deed the reward of the Hereafter, ﴿We will increase him in his tilth﴾, that is, in his good deeds. ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world﴾, that is, whoever is among the wicked who desires by his good deed this world, ﴿We will give him of it﴾. Then that was abrogated in Surat Subhan: ﴿Whoever desires the hastening [life], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We desire﴾ [al-Isra': 18]. The correct view is that this is not abrogation, because this is a report, and all things are by the will of God Mighty and Majestic. Do you not see that it is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "None of you should say: O God, forgive me if You wish; O God, have mercy on me if You wish." Qatadah has said what was mentioned earlier, and it clarifies for you that there is no abrogation. We have mentioned in (Surat) Hud that this is from the category of the absolute and the restricted, and that abrogation does not enter into reports [[See vol. 9, p. 14]]. And God is the One sought for help.

Issue: This verse invalidates the position of Abu Hanifah in his saying that whoever performs ablution merely for cooling down, it suffices for the obligatory ablution required of him, since the obligatory ablution is from the tilth of the Hereafter and cooling down is from the tilth of this world, so neither enters upon the other, and his intention does not suffice in its place by the apparent meaning of this verse. So said Ibn al-Arabi.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 21:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do they have partners﴾ meaning: "Do they have...?" The mim (م) is a connecting particle (silah), and the hamzah is for rebuke (taqri') . This is connected to His saying: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion that which He enjoined upon Nuh﴾ [al-Shura: 13], and His saying: ﴿Allah is the One who has sent down the Book with truth and the Balance﴾ [al-Shura: 17]. They did not believe in it. So do they have deities who have legislated for them polytheism, which Allah has not permitted? And if this is impossible, then Allah has not legislated polytheism, so from where do they derive their religion? "And had it not been for a decisive word" (on the Day of Resurrection, when He said: ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾ [al-Qamar: 46]) [[See vol. 17, p. 146.]] "it would have been judged between them" in this world, so He would have hastened the punishment for the wrongdoer and rewarded the obedient. "And indeed the wrongdoers" , i.e., the polytheists, "for them is a painful punishment": in this world, killing, captivity and subjugation, and in the Hereafter, the punishment of the Fire. Ibn Hurmuz read "wa-inna" with a fatha on the hamzah, as a conjunction (ataf) upon "wa-law la kalimatu," and the separation between the conjoined and the conjoined-to by the response of "law la" is permissible. It is also possible that the position of "inna" is nominative (raf'), on the estimate: "It is obligatory that the wrongdoers have a painful punishment," so it would be cut off from what precedes it, like the reading with kasra. So understand this.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned﴾, meaning: afraid, "of what they have earned," meaning: of the recompense for what they have earned. "The wrongdoers" here are the disbelievers, as evidenced by the division between the believer and the disbeliever. "And it will befall them," meaning: it will descend upon them. "But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of paradise." The (rawdah) is: a pleasant place abounding in greenery. It has already been mentioned in "al-Rum" [[see vol. 14, p. 11]]. "They will have whatever they wish with their Lord," meaning: of bliss and abundant reward. "That is the great bounty," meaning: it cannot be described, and minds cannot reach the reality of its attributes, because when the Truth says "great," who can measure its greatness?

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 23:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is what Allah gives good news of to His servants who believe﴾. It has been read as *yubashshiru* (with a doubled shin, from *bashshara*), as *yubshiru* (from *abshara*), and as *yabshuru* (from *bashara*). There is an ellipsis in it, meaning: Allah gives good news by it to His believing servants, so that they may hasten to joy and increase in their eagerness for obedience.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say, I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for my near kin﴾. On this there are two issues.

The first: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Say, I do not ask you any reward for it﴾, meaning: Say, O Muhammad, I do not ask you any wage for conveying the message. ﴿Except love for my near kin﴾. Al-Zajjaj (d. 311 AH), a grammarian and exegete, said: "Except love" is an exception that is not from the first part, meaning: except that you love me for my kinship, so that you protect me. The address is specifically to the Quraysh. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu Malik, al-Sha'bi and others. Al-Sha'bi said: "People argued against us about this verse, so we wrote to Ibn 'Abbas asking him about it. He wrote that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was of the middle lineage among the Quraysh, and there was no clan of theirs except that he was related to it. Then Allah said to him: ﴿Say, I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for my near kin﴾, meaning: except that you love me for my kinship with you, so that you observe what is between me and you and thus confirm me." Thus "*al-qurba*" here means the ties of kinship. It is as if he said: follow me for the sake of kinship, if you will not follow me for the sake of prophethood. 'Ikrimah said: "The Quraysh used to maintain their ties of kinship, but when the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, they severed them. So he said: (Maintain your ties with me as you used to do)." According to this meaning: "Say, I do not ask you any reward for it, but I remind you of my kinship." This is an exception that is not from the first part, as recorded by al-Nahhas (d. 338 AH), a grammarian and exegete.

In the Sahih of al-Bukhari, it is related from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he was asked about the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿except love for my near kin﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The kin of Muhammad." Ibn 'Abbas said: "You have been hasty! There was no clan of the Quraysh except that the Prophet (ﷺ) had kinship among them. So he said: except that you maintain the ties of kinship between you." This is one opinion.

It was also said: "*al-qurba*" means the kinship of the Messenger (ﷺ), meaning: I do not ask you any reward except that you love my kin and my family, just as he commanded honouring those of near kin. This is the view of 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb and al-Suddi. In the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Say, I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for my near kin﴾, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are these whom we should love?" He said: "'Ali, Fatima and their two sons." This is also supported by what is related from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I complained to the Prophet (ﷺ) of people's envy of me. He said: 'Are you not content to be the fourth of four, the first to enter Paradise: I, you, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and our wives on our right and left, and our offspring behind our wives?'" And from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Paradise is forbidden to whoever wrongs my family and harms me concerning my kin, and whoever does a favour to any of the sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib and does not repay it, I shall repay him for it tomorrow when he meets me on the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: the meaning is except that they seek closeness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and draw near to Him by obeying Him. According to this, "*al-qurba*" has the sense of "*al-qurba*" (nearness). It is said: *qurba* and *qurba* have the same meaning, like *zulfa* and *zulfa*.

Qaza'a ibn Suwayd related from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Say: I do not ask you any reward for what I have brought you, except that you love one another and draw near to Him through obedience."

Mansur and Awf related from al-Hasan concerning ﴿Say, I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for my near kin﴾: He said: "They seek the love of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and draw near to Him by obeying Him."

Some people said: the verse is abrogated (*mansukha*, subject to *naskh*, abrogation), and it was revealed in Makkah. The polytheists used to harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so this verse was revealed, and Allah commanded them to love His Prophet (ﷺ) and to maintain his ties of kinship. Then when he migrated, the Ansar sheltered him and supported him, and Allah wished to join him to his brethren among the Prophets, where they said: ﴿And I do not ask you any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:109].[[Verses 109, 127, 145, 164 and 180 of Surat al-Shu'ara'.]] Then Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Say, whatever reward I have asked of you is for yourselves; my reward is only from Allah﴾ [Saba' 34:47].[[Verse 47 of Surat Saba'.]] So it was abrogated by this verse, and by His saying: ﴿Say, I do not ask you any reward for it, and I am not of those who put on pretences﴾ [Sad 38:86],[[Verse 86 of Surat Sad.]] and His saying: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment, when the provision of your Lord is better?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:72],[[Verse 72 of Surat al-Mu'minun.]] and His saying: ﴿Or do you ask them for a wage, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ [al-Tur 52:40].[[Verse 40 of Surat al-Tur and verse 46 of Surat al-Qalam.]] This was said by al-Dahhak and al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl. Juwaybir related it from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Tha'labi said: "It is not strong. It is enough of an ugliness to say that drawing near to Allah through obedience to Him and love for His Prophet (ﷺ) and the People of his House is abrogated." The Prophet (ﷺ) has said: "Whoever dies upon love for the family of Muhammad dies as a martyr. Whoever dies upon love for the family of Muhammad, Allah makes the angels and mercy the visitors of his grave. Whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad will come on the Day of Resurrection with written between his eyes: 'Despairing of the mercy of Allah.' Whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad will not smell the fragrance of Paradise. Whoever dies upon hatred of the family of my House, there is no share for him in my intercession."[[i.e. he will not smell its fragrance. It is said: *rāḥa yurīḥ*, *rāḥa yurāḥ* and *arāḥa yurīḥ*; all three forms have been related for this hadith.]]

I say: al-Zamakhshari also mentioned this report in his tafsir, longer than this, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies upon love for the family of Muhammad dies as a martyr. Beware: whoever dies upon love for the family of Muhammad dies a believer whose faith is complete. Beware: whoever dies upon love for the family of Muhammad, the Angel of Death gives him good news of Paradise, then Munkar and Nakir. Beware: whoever dies upon love for the family of Muhammad, two doors to Paradise are opened for him in his grave. Beware: whoever dies in love for the family of Muhammad, Allah makes his grave a place visited by the angels of mercy. Beware: whoever dies upon love for the family of Muhammad dies upon the Sunnah and the community. Beware: whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad will come on the Day of Resurrection with written between his eyes: 'Despairing of the mercy of Allah.' Beware: whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad dies a disbeliever. Beware: whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad will not smell the fragrance of Paradise."

Al-Nahhas said: The view of 'Ikrimah is that it is not abrogated. He said: "They used to maintain their ties of kinship, but when the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, they severed them, so he said: (Say, I do not ask you any reward for it, except that you love me and protect me for my kinship and do not deny me)." I say: This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn 'Abbas in al-Bukhari and of al-Sha'bi from him, precisely; and according to it there is no abrogation.

Al-Nahhas said: The saying of al-Hasan is good, and its soundness is supported by the connected (*musnad*) hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Azdi told us, saying: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman al-Muradi told us, saying: Asad ibn Musa told us, saying: Qaza'a, who is Ibn Yazid[[It has been mentioned earlier that he is Qaza'a ibn Suwayd, who is among those who narrate from Ibn Abi Najih.

(See Tahdhib al-Tahdhib.)]] al-Basri, told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Najih told us, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I do not ask you any reward for the clear proofs and guidance that I convey to you, except that you love Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that you draw near to Him through obedience to Him." So this is the one who explains on behalf of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who has said this; and likewise the Prophets, peace be upon them, said before him: ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾ [Saba' 34:47].

The second issue: The scholars differed concerning the occasion of its revelation. Ibn 'Abbas said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Madinah, he was faced with calamities and rights that what was in his hands could not meet. So the Ansar said: "This man, Allah guided you through him, and he is your nephew, and calamities and rights befall him which what is in his hands cannot meet. So let us gather something for him." They did so, then brought it to him, and this verse was revealed. Al-Hasan said: It was revealed when the Ansar and the Muhajirun boasted to one another. The Ansar said: "We did (the most)." The Muhajirun boasted of their kinship with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Miqsam related from Ibn 'Abbas: He heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say something, then he addressed the Ansar and said: "Were you not humble, and Allah made you mighty through me? Were you not astray, and Allah guided you through me? Were you not fearful, and Allah gave you security through me? Will you not answer me?" They said: "With what shall we answer you?" He said: "Say: 'Did your people not drive you out, and we sheltered you? Did your people not deny you, and we confirmed you?'..." and he enumerated for them. He said: So they knelt upon their knees and said: "Our souls and our wealth are yours." Then this was revealed: "Say, I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the near kin."

Qatada said: The polytheists said: "Perhaps Muhammad, in what he undertakes, seeks a wage." So this verse was revealed, to urge them to love him and to love his relatives. Al-Tha'labi said: This is more fitting to the verse, because the surah is Makkan.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever earns a good deed﴾: meaning, whoever acquires it. The root of *qarf* is acquiring; it is said: "So-and-so *yaqrifu* for his dependants," meaning he earns. *Iqtiraf* is acquiring, and it is derived from their saying: "a man *qirfa*," when he is a schemer. The discussion of this has already passed in "al-An'am".[[See vol. 7, p. 70.]] Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿And whoever earns a good deed﴾ is the love for the family of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿We shall increase for him in its goodness﴾, meaning we shall multiply the good deed by ten or more. ﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾. Qatada said: "Forgiving" of sins, "Appreciative" of good deeds. Al-Suddi said: "Forgiving" of the sins of the family of Muhammad, peace be upon him, "Appreciative" of their good deeds.

**The commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 42, verse 24:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against God"?﴾ The *mim* (*al-mīm*, here an extra connecting particle, *ṣila*) is redundant, and the implied reading is *a-yaqūlūna iftarā* ("Do they say he has invented?"). The speech is connected to what precedes it, because when God, Exalted is He, said, ﴿Say, "I believe in whatever Book God has sent down"﴾ [[Verse 15 of this surah.]] [al-Shura: 15], and said, ﴿God is He who sent down the Book with truth﴾ [[Verse 17 of this surah.]] [al-Shura: 17], He said, to complete the explanation: "Or do they say, 'He has invented a lie against God'?" meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh said, "Muhammad has fabricated the lie against God." Then ﴿If God wills, He would seal﴾ is a conditional, and its answer is ﴿upon your heart﴾. Qatadah said: He would seal upon your heart, so that He would make you forget the Qur'an. God thus informed them that if he (Muhammad) had invented against Him, He would do to Muhammad what He informed them of in this verse. Mujahid and Muqatil said: ﴿If God wills﴾ means He would bind your heart with patience in bearing their harm, so that no distress from their words would enter your heart. It was also said: the meaning is, if He wills, He would remove your discernment. It was also said: the meaning is, if you were to entertain in yourself the thought of fabricating a lie against God, your heart would be sealed; this was said by Ibn 'Isa. It was also said: ﴿If God wills, He would seal﴾ means He would seal the hearts and tongues of the disbelievers and hasten their punishment. Thus the address is to him, while the intended meaning is the disbelievers; this was mentioned by al-Qushayri.

Then he began, saying: ﴿And God will efface falsehood﴾. Ibn al-Anbari said: ﴿He would seal upon your heart﴾ is a complete clause. Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion in it, its sense being "And God effaces falsehood," and the *waw* was omitted from it in the codex, though it is in the position of a nominative. This is like the omission of it in His saying, ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ [[Verse 18 of Surah al-'Alaq.]] [al-'Alaq: 18], and ﴿And man supplicates﴾ [al-Isra': 11]. It is also because it is coordinated with His saying, ﴿He would seal upon your heart﴾.

Al-Zajjaj said: His saying, ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against God"?﴾ is complete, and His saying, ﴿And God will efface falsehood﴾ is an argument against those who deny what the Prophet (ﷺ) brought: that is, if what he brought were falsehood, God would efface it, as is His custom with fabricators. ﴿And establishes the truth﴾, that is, Islam, so He establishes it ﴿by His words﴾, that is, by what He sent down of the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed He is Knower of what is in the breasts﴾ is general, that is, of what is in the hearts of His servants. It was also said that it is specific. The meaning is that if you were to entertain in yourself the thought of fabricating a lie against God, He would know it and seal upon your heart.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 25:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: When the saying of the Exalted, "Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin" [Q. 42:23], was revealed, a people said within themselves: "He only wants to urge us toward his relatives after him." Jibril informed the Prophet ﷺ that they had accused him, and [Allah] revealed: "Or do they say, 'He has invented a lie against Allah'?" [Q. 42:24], the verse. The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, we testify that you are truthful, and we repent." Then it was revealed: "And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants." Ibn 'Abbas said: That is, from His friends and the people of His obedience. The verse is general. The discussion of the meaning of repentance (tawbah) and its rulings has already passed [see vol. 5, p. 90 and following]. This wording has also occurred in "Bara'ah" [verse 104, see vol. 8, p. (250)]: "and pardons the evil deeds," that is, the polytheism before Islam. "And He knows what you do," that is, of good and evil.

Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Hafs and Khalaf read the verb with the ta' (tafa'alu, second person, addressing the audience), and this is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and his companions. The rest read it with the ya' (third person, narrative). Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this, because it comes between two statements: the first, "And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants," and the second, "And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds."

"Those who believe" is in the accusative position, meaning: "And Allah responds to those who believe," that is, He accepts the worship of one who sincerely devotes it to Him with his heart and obeys with his body. It was also said: He gives them their request when they call upon Him. It was also said: "And He answers the supplication of the believers for one another," as it is said: ajaba (to answer) and istajaba (to respond) have the same meaning. This has already been discussed in al-Baqarah [see vol. 2, p. 308 onward, second edition].

Ibn Abbas said: "And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds" means He intercedes for them on behalf of their brothers. "And He increases them of His bounty" — he said: He intercedes for them on behalf of the brothers of their brothers.

Al-Mubarrad said: the meaning of "And He responds to those who believe" is "And let those who believe seek a response," this being the literal meaning of the form istaf'ala. In this case, "those who believe" is in the nominative position.

"And the disbelievers, for them is a severe punishment."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 27:

There are two issues here.

The first concerns the occasion of its revelation. It has been said: it was revealed concerning a group from the People of the Suffah (ahl al-Suffah, the poor companions who lived in the shaded area of the Prophet's mosque) who wished for abundance of provision. Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: it was revealed concerning us. We looked at the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir, Quraydhah and Banu Qaynuqa', we wished for it, and so it was revealed.

﴿Had Allah expanded the provision for His servants, they would have transgressed in the earth﴾. "Basata" means he expanded (wassa'a). And "basata al-shay'" means he spread it out; it is also read with the sad (basat). "Labaghaw fi al-ard" means they would have become insolent and disobedient.

Ibn Abbas said: their "baghy" (transgression) is their seeking one station after another, one mount after another, one vehicle after another, and one garment after another.

It has also been said: he meant that if He gave them much, they would seek what is more than it, based on his saying (ﷺ): "If the son of Adam had two valleys of gold, he would seek a third." This is baghy, and it is the meaning of Ibn Abbas's words.

It has also been said: if We made them equal in wealth, some would not submit to others, and the crafts would be idle.

It has also been said: by "provision" he meant the rain, which is the cause of provision; that is, if He kept the rain constant, they would be occupied with it and turn away from supplication. Thus He withholds at times so that they may humble themselves, and extends at other times so that they may give thanks.

It has also been said: when they had abundance, some of them would raid others. So it is not far-fetched to take baghy in this sense.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "labaghaw" is from baghy, which is injustice; that is, one would wrong the other and the other would wrong him, because wealth causes arrogance and insolence, and Qarun suffices as a lesson.

From this is his (ﷺ) saying: "What I fear most for my community is the splendour of this world and its abundance."

And a poet of the Arabs said:

"The early rain has made growth appear between us
and between the Banu Dudan, sanctuary and shawhat."

[Note: al-wasmi is the rain of early spring. The nab' and shawhat are mountain trees from which bows are made. In the original manuscripts and some books of tafsir: "...Banu Rumān." Dudan is the father of a tribe of Asad.]

That is, they came to life and then spoke to themselves of transgression and deception.

Or it is from baghy, which means haughtiness and pride; that is, they would become arrogant on the earth and do what follows pride of elevation and corruption in it.

﴿But He sends down in measured amount what He wills﴾: that is, He sends down their provisions in the measure He wills, sufficient for them. Muqatil said: "He sends down in measured amount what He wills" means He makes whom He wills rich and whom He wills poor.

The second issue: Our scholars said: the acts of the Lord, glory be to Him, are never devoid of wisdoms, even though it is not obligatory upon Allah to act for what is best. He may know from the state of a servant that if wealth were expanded for him it would lead him to corruption, so He withholds the world from him, as a benefit for him. Hence narrowness of provision is not humiliation, nor is abundance a virtue. He has given to peoples while knowing that they would use it in corruption, and had He done otherwise with them they would have been closer to righteousness. The matter in general is entrusted to His will, and it is not possible to bind every act of Allah to the doctrine of what is best.

Anas narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ), on what he relates from his Lord, blessed and exalted, that he said: "Whoever humiliates a friend of Mine has declared war against Me. I am swiftest of all things in aiding My friends, and I become angry for them as the fierce lion becomes angry. I do not hesitate in anything I do as I hesitate in taking the soul of My believing servant, who dislikes death, and I dislike to harm him, yet it is inevitable for him. My believing servant does not draw near to Me with anything like performing what I have obligated upon him. My believing servant continues to draw near to Me by voluntary acts until I love him; when I love him, I am his hearing, his sight, his tongue, his hand, and his support. If he asks Me, I give him; if he calls upon Me, I answer him.
