On this basis, Ibn Zayd said: all of this is abrogated by jihad, and this applies to the polytheists specifically. Qatadah's view is that it is general, and the apparent meaning of the statement supports this. We have explained this, praise be to Allah.

The seventh point: Ibn al-'Arabi said: this verse corresponds to the earlier verse in Bara'ah, which is His saying ﴿There is no path [of blame] against the doers of good﴾ [At-Tawbah: 91]. Just as Allah negated the path against those who do good, so He affirmed it against those who wrong, and He completed the explanation of both categories.

The eighth point: Our scholars differed regarding a ruler who imposes a fixed sum on the people of a city, collecting it from them and having them pay it according to their wealth. Is it permissible for one who is able to escape this to do so, while in that case the rest of the people of the city are taken for the full amount imposed on them? It was said: no, and this is the view of Sahnun from our scholars. It was said: yes, he may do so if he is able to escape, and this is the view of Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Nasr al-Dawudi, then the Maliki. He said: what supports this is Malik's statement concerning the collector who takes a sheep from the flock of one of the partners when the flock as a whole does not reach the minimum: it is an injustice upon the one from whom it was taken, and he has no recourse against his partners for anything. He said: I do not adopt what is narrated from Sahnun, because injustice has no parallel, and no one is obliged to thrust himself into injustice for fear that the injustice will be multiplied upon others. Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿The path is only against those who wrong the people﴾.

The ninth point: The scholars differed regarding halalah (granting release/forgiveness of debt or wrong). Ibn al-Musayyib would not grant release to anyone regarding honour or property. Sulayman ibn Yasar and Muhammad ibn Sirin would grant release regarding both honour and property. Malik held that release is permitted regarding property but not regarding honour. Ibn al-Qasim and Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik, when he was asked about the statement of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, "I do not grant release to anyone," that he said: "That differs." I said to him: "O Abu 'Abd Allah, a man lends to another man and he perishes with no means of repayment?" He said: "I think he should release him, and that is better in my view, for Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Those who listen to the word and follow the best of it﴾ [Az-Zumar: 18]." It was said to him: "A man wrongs a man?" He said: "I do not think that. In my view it contradicts the first. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿The path is only against those who wrong the people﴾, and He, exalted is He, says: ﴿There is no path against the doers of good﴾ [At-Tawbah: 91]. So I do not think he should make it lawful for him from his injustice." Ibn al-'Arabi said: thus there are three views on the question. The first: he should not release him under any circumstances; this was said by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib. The second: he should release him; this was said by Muhammad ibn Sirin. The third: if it is property, he releases him, and if it is injustice, he does not release him; this is the view of Malik. The reasoning of the first is that one should not make lawful what Allah has forbidden, as that would amount to altering the ruling of Allah. The reasoning of the second is that it is his right, so he may waive it just as he may waive his blood and honour. The reasoning of the third, which Malik chose, is that when a man is unable to fulfil your right, it is kindness to him to release him; but if he is a wrongdoer, it is right not to leave him, lest the wrongdoers be emboldened (in some manuscripts: "and conceal themselves"; in others: "and seek counsel") and proceed in their ugly deeds. In Sahih Muslim is the lengthy hadith of Abu al-Yusr, in which he said to his debtor: "Come out to me, for I know where you are." So he came out, and he said: "What prevented you from hiding from me?" He said: "By Allah, I will tell you and not lie to you. I feared by Allah that I would tell you and lie, and that I would promise you and break it. You were a companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and by Allah I was in hardship." He said: "I said: 'By Allah?'" He said: "By Allah." He said: "Then he brought a document and erased it, and said: 'If you find the means to pay, then pay; otherwise you are released...'" and he mentioned the hadith. Ibn al-'Arabi said: this applies to the living one from whom payment is hoped, for the sake of the soundness of his obligation and the hope of his finding a way out; so how about the dead one who has no means of release and no obligation remaining with him?

The tenth point: Some scholars said: whoever is wronged and has property taken from him, he has only the reward of what was withheld from him until his death; then the reward passes to his heirs, and so on to the last of them, because the property passes after him to the heir. Abu Ja'far al-Dawudi al-Maliki said: this is sound in reasoning, and according to this view, if the wrongdoer dies before the one he wronged and leaves nothing, or leaves what his heir does not know to be unjust, the claim of the wronged person does not transfer to the heirs of the wrongdoer, because nothing remains with the wrongdoer that his heirs of the wronged person could claim.

(Marginal note) The eleventh point: Allah's saying ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives﴾ means: he bears harm patiently, and "forgives" means he leaves retaliation for the sake of Allah, the Exalted; this applies to one who is wronged by a Muslim. It is related that a man insulted another man in the gathering of al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, and the one insulted kept his anger in and perspired, and wiped the sweat; then he stood up and recited this verse. Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, he understood it and grasped it, when the ignorant ones neglected it." In sum, pardon is recommended, though in some circumstances the matter may be reversed, so that refraining from pardon becomes recommended, as mentioned earlier; this is when it is necessary to restrain the increase of aggression and cut off the source of harm. There is a report from the Prophet ﷺ indicating this: that Zaynab reviled 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with them both, in his presence, and he kept forbidding her but she did not desist, so he said to 'A'ishah: "Go ahead and retaliate." Muslim recorded it in his Sahih in this meaning. It was also said: "patience" is restraint from sins and concealment of faults. ﴿Indeed, that is of the steadfast matters﴾ means: of the determinations of Allah which He commanded. It was also said: of the determinations of right conduct to which one is granted success.

Al-Kalbi and al-Farra' mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, together with the three verses before it; one of the Ansar had reviled him, and he responded, then he refrained. These are the Madani verses of this surah. It was also said: these verses concern the polytheists, and this was at the beginning of Islam before the command to fight, then the verse of fighting abrogated them; this is the view of Ibn Zayd, and it has been mentioned earlier.

In the tafsir of Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And whoever takes revenge after being wronged﴾ refers to Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, 'Ubaydah, 'Ali and all the Muhajirun, may Allah be pleased with them. ﴿Those, there is no path against them﴾ refers to Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, 'Ubaydah and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them all. ﴿The path is only against those who wrong the people﴾ refers to 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, al-Walid ibn 'Utbah, Abu Jahl and al-Aswad, and every polytheist who fought on the day of Badr. ﴿And they seek to cause corruption in the earth﴾ refers to by injustice and disbelief. ﴿For them is a painful punishment﴾ refers to a painful one. ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives﴾ refers to Abu Bakr, 'Umar, Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr and all the people of Badr, may Allah be pleased with them all. ﴿Indeed, that is of the steadfast matters﴾ refers to their accepting ransom and their patience over harm.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 44:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no protector after Him﴾, i.e., He forsakes him. "For him there is no protector after Him." This applies to the one who turned away from the Prophet ﷺ in what he invited him to of faith in Allah and love for the near of kin, and did not believe him regarding the Resurrection and that the enjoyment of this world is little. That is, whomever Allah has led astray from these matters, no guide will guide him.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you will see the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., the disbelievers. "When they see the punishment," meaning Hellfire. It was also said: they see the punishment at the time of death. "They say, 'Is there any way to return?'" They seek to be returned to the world so that they may act in obedience to Allah, but they will not be granted that.

Qur'an 42:45 — "And you will see them presented to it (the Fire)..." Al-Qurtubi's words: God's saying, "And you will see them presented to it" means: to the Fire, because it is their punishment. So the feminine pronoun refers to the punishment just mentioned, because that punishment is the Fire; and if you wish, it is Jahannam (Hell). Had he observed the wording, he would have said "upon it" (ʿalayhi, masculine). Then it has been said: they are all the polytheists, who are presented to Jahannam when they are driven toward it; this is the view of the majority. It has also been said: specifically the family of Pharaoh, whose spirits are held in the bodies of black birds that go to Jahannam in the morning and return in the evening; so their being presented to it is this, and this is what Ibn Mas'ud said. It has also been said: they are the polytheists in general, whose sins are displayed to them in their graves, and they are presented to punishment in their graves; and this is the meaning of the saying of Abu al-Hajjaj.

"Humbled from abasement" — some reciters held that one should pause at "khashiʿīn" (humbled). The phrase "min al-dhull" (from abasement) is then connected to "yanẓurūn" (they look). It has also been said that it is connected to "khashiʿīn." Khushūʿ means humbling oneself and lowliness.

The meaning of "they look from a hidden glance" (min ṭarfin khafiyy) is that they do not raise their eyes to look fully, because they are bowed of head. The Arabs describe the abased person by lowering the glance, just as they use, in its opposite, "sharp gaze" for one who is not accused of a suspicion, so that no humiliation falls on him from it. Mujahid said: "from a hidden glance" means abased. He said: they look only with their hearts, because they are gathered blind, and the eye of the heart is a hidden glance. Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Qurazi and Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: they steal glances out of intense fear. It has also been said: the meaning is that they look with a weak eye. Yunus said: "min" here means "bi" (with), i.e., they look with a hidden, weak glance out of abasement and fear; and similar is reported from al-Akhfash. Ibn ʿAbbas said: with a faint, abased glance. It has also been said: that is, they dread looking at it with the full sight of their eyes, because of the kinds of punishment they see.

"And those who believed will say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection." That is, the believers in Paradise will say, when they witness what has befallen the disbelievers: indeed the true loss is what these people have come to, for they have lost themselves because they are in everlasting punishment, and they have lost their families, because if the families are in the Fire there is no benefit in them, and if they are in Paradise, then a barrier has been placed between them and them. It has also been said: the loss of the family is that, had they believed, they would have had families in Paradise among the wide-eyed houris.

In the Sunan of Ibn Majah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "There is none of you but he has two abodes: an abode in Paradise and an abode in the Fire. When he dies and enters the Fire, the people of Paradise inherit his abode. That is the saying of God: ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾ [al-Muminun: 10]." This has been mentioned before.

In the Musnad of al-Darimi, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "There is no one whom God admits to Paradise except that He marries him to seventy-two wives from the wide-eyed houris, and seventy from the inheritance of his from the people of the Fire; and not one of them but has a sweet vagina, and he has a member that does not slacken." Hisham ibn Khalid said: "from the inheritance of his from the people of the Fire" means men who were admitted into the Fire, so the people of Paradise inherit their wives, just as the wife of Pharaoh was inherited.

"Verily, the wrongdoers are in a lasting punishment" — that is, perpetual, never ending. Then it is permissible that this is the speech of the believers, and it is permissible that it is a beginning from God, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 46:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they will have no protectors (awliya') to help them﴾, that is, helpers and supporters, "who will support them against Allah," that is, against His punishment. "And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no way (sabil)," that is, no path that leads him to the truth in this world or to Paradise in the Hereafter, because the path of salvation has been closed off to him.

"The Almighty's saying: ﴿Respond to your Lord﴾, meaning: answer Him in what He has called you to, namely faith in Him and obedience. Istajaba (to respond) and ajaba (to answer) have the same meaning, as has already been discussed. ﴿Before there comes a Day which there is no turning back from, from Allah﴾ means the Day of Resurrection, i.e., no one can turn it back after Allah has decreed it and made it an appointed term and time. ﴿You will have no refuge﴾, meaning no refuge that will save you from the punishment. ﴿Nor will you have any denial﴾, meaning no helper who will help you. This was said by Mujahid. It was also said that nakir has the meaning of munkar (denied, rejected), like alim in the sense of mu'lim (painful). That is, on that day you will not find anyone to deny what punishment befalls you. This was related by Ibn Abi Hatim, and was said by al-Kalbi. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is that they will not be able to deny the sins for which they are held to account. It was also said: ﴿nakir﴾ means the denial of what punishment befalls you, and nakir and inkar (denial) mean changing the wrong (munkar)."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 48:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But if they turn away﴾, meaning from faith, ﴿then We have not sent you as a watcher over them﴾, meaning a guardian of their deeds, so that you would call them to account for them. It was also said: one entrusted with them, who does not leave them until they believe, meaning it is not for you to compel them to faith. ﴿Your duty is only to convey (the message)﴾. It was also said: this was abrogated by the verse of fighting (naskh, abrogation, meaning the later ruling replaces the earlier one). ﴿And when We let man taste mercy from Us﴾, meaning the disbelieving man, ﴿he rejoices in it﴾, meaning he exults in it. ﴿But if an evil befalls them﴾, meaning affliction and hardship, ﴿because of what their hands have sent forward, then indeed man is ungrateful﴾, meaning for the blessing that came before, so he enumerates the calamities and forgets the blessings.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 42, verses 49–50 (part 1 of 2)**

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills﴾. On this there are four issues.

The first issue: Allah the Exalted's words ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ are a mubtada' (subject) and a khabar (predicate). "He creates what He wills" means of creation. "He bestows females on whom He wills and bestows males on whom He wills." Abu Ubayda, Abu Malik, Mujahid, al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: He bestows females on whom He wills, with no males among them, and bestows males on whom He wills, with no females among them. The definite article (al-) was attached to "males" but not to "females," because males are more honoured, so He distinguished them with the mark of definiteness. Wathila ibn al-Asqa' said: "Among the blessings of a woman is that she bears a female before a male, because Allah the Exalted said: 'He bestows females on whom He wills and bestows males on whom He wills,' and He began with females."

"Or He pairs them, males and females." Mujahid said: this means that a woman gives birth to a boy, then to a girl, then to a boy, then to a girl. Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya said: it means that she gives birth to twins, a boy and a girl. "Or He pairs them, males and females." Al-Qutabi said: "pairing" (tazwij) here means combining sons and daughters. The Arabs say: "I paired my camels" when I combined the large and the small.

"And He makes barren whom He wills": that is, he will not have children. One says: "a man is 'aqim (barren), and a woman is 'aqim." The woman became barren (ta'qam 'aqman), like hamida yahmadu, and she became barren (ta'qum), like 'azuma ya'zumu. The root meaning is cutting off. From it comes "the barren kingdom" (al-mulk al-'aqim), in which the wombs are cut off through killing and disobedience out of fear for the kingdom. A "barren wind" (rih 'aqim) is one that does not fertilise clouds or trees. The Day of Resurrection is a "barren day" ('aqim) because there is no day after it. It is said: "barren women" ('uqum and 'uqm). The poet said [[In Lisan al-Arab: "Abu Dahbal said, praising 'Abd Allah ibn al-Azraq al-Makhzumi. It is said it belongs to al-Huzayn al-Laythi."]]:

"The women have become barren, so they do not bear one like him;
Indeed the women are barren of his like."

Al-Naqqash related that this verse was revealed especially concerning the prophets, though its ruling is general. Lot was given females with no males among them. Abraham was given males with no females among them. Isma'il and Isaac were given both males and females. 'Isa and Yahya were made barren. Similar was reported from Ibn 'Abbas and Ishaq ibn Bishr. Ishaq said: it was revealed concerning the prophets, and then it became general.

"He bestows females on whom He wills": meaning Lot, peace be upon him. No male was born to him; he had only two daughters. "And bestows males on whom He wills": meaning Abraham, peace be upon him. No female was born to him; rather eight males were born to him. "Or He pairs them, males and females": meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to whom four sons and four daughters were born. "And He makes barren whom He wills": meaning Yahya ibn Zakariyya, peace be upon them both; 'Isa is not mentioned.

Ibn al-'Arabi said: Our scholars said: "He bestows females on whom He wills" means Lot, who had daughters and no son. "And bestows males on whom He wills" means Abraham, who had sons and no daughter. As for "Or He pairs them, males and females," it means Adam, to whom Eve gave birth in every litter twins, a male and a female; and he paired the male of one litter with the female of another litter, until Allah confirmed the prohibition in the law of Noah (ﷺ). Likewise Muhammad (ﷺ) had male and female children: al-Qasim, al-Tayyib, al-Tahir, 'Abd Allah [[The more correct view is that the males were three: al-Qasim, 'Abd Allah (also called al-Tayyib and al-Tahir), and Ibrahim. See Sharh al-Mawahib al-Ladunniyya.]], Zaynab, Umm Kulthum, Ruqayya and Fatima, all of them from Khadija (may Allah be pleased with her), and Ibrahim, who was from Maria the Copt. Likewise Allah has apportioned creation from the time of Adam until our present age, and until the Hour arrives, according to this limited measure, by His perfect wisdom and His executing will, so that the offspring may remain, creation may continue, the promise may be fulfilled, the matter may be decreed, the world may be populated, and Paradise and Hell may each take what fills it and remains. There is a hadith: "Hell will not be filled until the Almighty places His foot in it [[Al-Qastallani said: 'That is, He humbles it, the humbling of one who is placed under the foot; the Arabs use body parts for figurative meaning and do not mean the parts themselves, as when they say of one who regrets: "He fell into his hand."']], and it says: 'Qat, qat' [[The word "qat qat" may be read with the ta' vowelled or sukun, and both are permitted. With kasra it may be read with tanwin. The meaning is: enough for me, enough for me, I have had enough.']]. As for Paradise, some of it remains, and Allah creates for it another creation."

The second issue: Ibn al-'Arabi said: Allah the Exalted, by the generality of His power and the intensity of His might, creates creation ex nihilo without any prior material; and by the greatness of His subtle kindness and the perfection of His wisdom, He creates one thing from another, not out of need, for He is holy (quddus) above needs and free from defects (salam), as He said: "the Holy, the Peace." So He created Adam from the earth, created Eve from Adam, and created offspring from both of them, arranged upon intercourse, existing as a result of conception, present in the foetus through delivery. As the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the man's water precedes the woman's water, the child is male; and when the woman's water precedes the man's water, the child is female" [[It is narrated with the alif (a long vowel) and light nun, and also with the short vowel and doubled nun.]]. Likewise in the Sahih as well: "When the man's water prevails over the woman's water, the child resembles his paternal uncles; and when the woman's water prevails over the man's water, the child resembles his maternal uncles."

I say: this is the meaning of the hadith of 'A'isha, not its wording. Muslim transmitted it from the narration of 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr from her: a woman said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Does a woman perform ghusl if she has a wet dream and sees the fluid?" He said: "Yes." 'A'isha said to her: "May your hands be dusted and may you be ..." [[The phrase "tariat yadaka" means: may you not succeed! Originally it means that dust has come onto your hand, and that you did not attain any good, i.e., you became poor. But they do not intend by it a curse upon the one addressed, as they say: "May Allah fight him," and so on. The phrase "wa allat" means she cried out because of the severity of this statement. It is also narrated with a damma on the hamza and doubled lam, meaning she was pierced by the arguments, which is a spear. Ibn al-Athir said: this is far-fetched, because it does not suit the wording of the hadith.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let her be. Does resemblance come from anything other than that? When the woman's fluid prevails over the man's fluid, the child resembles his maternal uncles; and when the man's fluid prevails over hers, the child resembles his paternal uncles."

Our scholars said: according to the requirement of this hadith, prevalence necessitates resemblance. It has also come in the hadith of Thawban, which Muslim also transmitted, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the Jew: "The man's water is white and the woman's water is yellow. When the two combine, if the man's semen prevails over the woman's semen, it is male by the permission of Allah; and if the woman's semen prevails over the man's semen, it is female by the permission of Allah..."

...(the hadith). He also made, in this hadith, the "uluw" (here, precedence or superiority) entail maleness and femaleness. Thus, according to the two hadiths, it would follow that if the man's water prevails, the child resembles his paternal uncles and is male, and likewise, if the woman's water prevails, the child resembles its maternal uncles and is female, because the two are effects of one cause. But the matter is not so. Rather, what is observed is contrary to this, for we find children resembling their maternal uncles and being male, and resembling their paternal uncles and being female. Therefore, one of the two hadiths must be interpreted. The one that must be interpreted is the hadith of Thawban. It is said: that "uluw" means that the water reached the womb first. Its basis is that "uluw," when its meaning is domination, comes from their saying: "So-and-so outran me (sabaqani), so I outran him (sabaqtuhu)," meaning I overcame him. From this is the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿And We are not to be outrun﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 60], meaning, not overcome. It was said [in the sense of] "he overcame him," "he prevailed." This interpretation is supported by his saying in the hadith: "If the man's water precedes the woman's water, the child is male, and if the woman's water precedes the man's water, the child is female."

Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi built upon these hadiths a structure. He said: The two waters have four states: First, the man's water comes out first. Second, the woman's water comes out first. Third, the man's water comes out first and is more abundant. Fourth, the woman's water comes out first and is more abundant. The division is completed by the man's water coming out first and then the woman's water coming out after it and being more abundant, or the reverse. So if the man's water comes out first and is more abundant, the child is male by the rule of precedence, and it resembles its paternal uncles by the rule of abundance. If the woman's water comes out first and is more abundant, the child is female by the rule of precedence, and it resembles its maternal uncles by the rule of dominance. If the man's water comes out first, but then the woman's water comes out after it and is more abundant, the child is male by the rule of precedence and resembles its maternal uncles by the rule of the dominance of the woman's water. If the woman's water comes out first, but then the man's water comes out and is higher than the woman's water, the child is female by the rule of the precedence of the woman's water, and resembles its paternal uncles by the rule of the dominance of the man's water. He said: By arranging these divisions, the discourse is set in order, the contradiction among the hadiths is removed, so glory be to the Creator, the All-Knowing.

The third matter: Our scholars said: The creation was consistently male and female until, in the first Jahiliyyah, the khuntha (the hermaphrodite, one of indeterminate sex) occurred. He was brought to 'Amir ibn al-Zarib, the chief and the one of the Arabs relied upon (it is said that he lived three hundred years), and he did not know what to say about him, and he deferred them concerning him. When night fell upon him, his place became strange to him, his bed was disturbed for him, and he kept tossing and turning, and thoughts came to him and went, until his servant noticed his condition and said: "What is wrong with you?" He said to her: "I have stayed awake over a matter I intended, and I do not know what to say about it." She said: "What is it?" He said to her: "A man who has a penis and a vulva, what is his status in inheritance?" The maidservant said to him: "Give him an inheritance according to where he urinates." So he understood her and in the morning he presented it to them, and they returned satisfied with it. Islam came upon that, and it did not descend (as a ruling) except in the time of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who judged regarding it.

The faraid scholars narrated, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he was asked about a newborn that has a front passage and a penis: "From where does he inherit?" He said: "From where he urinates." It is also narrated that a khuntha from the Ansar was brought, and he said: "Give him an inheritance from where he first urinates." Likewise Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah narrated from 'Ali, and similar from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn al-Musayyab, Abu Hanifah, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said the same, and al-Muzani related it from al-Shafi'i. Some people said: There is no indication in urination. If urine comes out from both, Abu Yusuf said: The judgment is according to the greater amount. Abu Hanifah rejected this and said: "Are you going to weigh it?" The companions of al-Shafi'i did not assign a ruling to abundance. It is related from 'Ali and al-Hasan that they said: His ribs are counted, for the woman has one rib more than the man. What the scholars said on this has already passed in the verse of inheritance in "an-Nisa'," thoroughly, and praise be to Allah.

The fourth matter: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said: Some of the leading common people denied the existence of the khuntha, because Allah Most High divided creation into male and female. We say: This is ignorance of the language, heedlessness of the eloquence of its structure, and a failure to grasp the breadth of power. As for the power of Allah, glory be to Him, He is Vast and All-Knowing. As for the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, it does not negate the existence of the khuntha, for Allah Most High said: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills﴾. This is a general praise, so it may not be restricted, because power requires it. As for His saying: ﴿He bestows females on whom He wills, and bestows males on whom He wills. Or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes whom He wills barren﴾, this is a report about the general case among existing beings, and it remained silent about mentioning the rare case, because it falls under the generality of the first statement. Existence bears witness to it, and direct observation refutes the one who denies it. With us, at the ribat of Abu Sa'id, in the presence of the martyr imam from the lands of the Maghrib, there was a khuntha who read with us. He had no beard, had two breasts, and had a female slave. Your Lord knows best about him. Despite long companionship, shyness prevented me from asking him, and today I wish I had uncovered his condition.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 42, verses 49–50 (part 1 of 2)**

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills﴾. On this there are four issues.

The first issue: Allah the Exalted's words ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ are a mubtada' (subject) and a khabar (predicate). "He creates what He wills" means of creation. "He bestows females on whom He wills and bestows males on whom He wills." Abu Ubayda, Abu Malik, Mujahid, al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: He bestows females on whom He wills, with no males among them, and bestows males on whom He wills, with no females among them. The definite article (al-) was attached to "males" but not to "females," because males are more honoured, so He distinguished them with the mark of definiteness. Wathila ibn al-Asqa' said: "Among the blessings of a woman is that she bears a female before a male, because Allah the Exalted said: 'He bestows females on whom He wills and bestows males on whom He wills,' and He began with females."

"Or He pairs them, males and females." Mujahid said: this means that a woman gives birth to a boy, then to a girl, then to a boy, then to a girl. Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya said: it means that she gives birth to twins, a boy and a girl. "Or He pairs them, males and females." Al-Qutabi said: "pairing" (tazwij) here means combining sons and daughters. The Arabs say: "I paired my camels" when I combined the large and the small.

"And He makes barren whom He wills": that is, he will not have children. One says: "a man is 'aqim (barren), and a woman is 'aqim." The woman became barren (ta'qam 'aqman), like hamida yahmadu, and she became barren (ta'qum), like 'azuma ya'zumu. The root meaning is cutting off. From it comes "the barren kingdom" (al-mulk al-'aqim), in which the wombs are cut off through killing and disobedience out of fear for the kingdom. A "barren wind" (rih 'aqim) is one that does not fertilise clouds or trees. The Day of Resurrection is a "barren day" ('aqim) because there is no day after it. It is said: "barren women" ('uqum and 'uqm). The poet said [[In Lisan al-Arab: "Abu Dahbal said, praising 'Abd Allah ibn al-Azraq al-Makhzumi. It is said it belongs to al-Huzayn al-Laythi."]]:

"The women have become barren, so they do not bear one like him;
Indeed the women are barren of his like."

Al-Naqqash related that this verse was revealed especially concerning the prophets, though its ruling is general. Lot was given females with no males among them. Abraham was given males with no females among them. Isma'il and Isaac were given both males and females. 'Isa and Yahya were made barren. Similar was reported from Ibn 'Abbas and Ishaq ibn Bishr. Ishaq said: it was revealed concerning the prophets, and then it became general.

"He bestows females on whom He wills": meaning Lot, peace be upon him. No male was born to him; he had only two daughters. "And bestows males on whom He wills": meaning Abraham, peace be upon him. No female was born to him; rather eight males were born to him. "Or He pairs them, males and females": meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to whom four sons and four daughters were born. "And He makes barren whom He wills": meaning Yahya ibn Zakariyya, peace be upon them both; 'Isa is not mentioned.

Ibn al-'Arabi said: Our scholars said: "He bestows females on whom He wills" means Lot, who had daughters and no son. "And bestows males on whom He wills" means Abraham, who had sons and no daughter. As for "Or He pairs them, males and females," it means Adam, to whom Eve gave birth in every litter twins, a male and a female; and he paired the male of one litter with the female of another litter, until Allah confirmed the prohibition in the law of Noah (ﷺ). Likewise Muhammad (ﷺ) had male and female children: al-Qasim, al-Tayyib, al-Tahir, 'Abd Allah [[The more correct view is that the males were three: al-Qasim, 'Abd Allah (also called al-Tayyib and al-Tahir), and Ibrahim. See Sharh al-Mawahib al-Ladunniyya.]], Zaynab, Umm Kulthum, Ruqayya and Fatima, all of them from Khadija (may Allah be pleased with her), and Ibrahim, who was from Maria the Copt. Likewise Allah has apportioned creation from the time of Adam until our present age, and until the Hour arrives, according to this limited measure, by His perfect wisdom and His executing will, so that the offspring may remain, creation may continue, the promise may be fulfilled, the matter may be decreed, the world may be populated, and Paradise and Hell may each take what fills it and remains. There is a hadith: "Hell will not be filled until the Almighty places His foot in it [[Al-Qastallani said: 'That is, He humbles it, the humbling of one who is placed under the foot; the Arabs use body parts for figurative meaning and do not mean the parts themselves, as when they say of one who regrets: "He fell into his hand."']], and it says: 'Qat, qat' [[The word "qat qat" may be read with the ta' vowelled or sukun, and both are permitted. With kasra it may be read with tanwin. The meaning is: enough for me, enough for me, I have had enough.']]. As for Paradise, some of it remains, and Allah creates for it another creation."

The second issue: Ibn al-'Arabi said: Allah the Exalted, by the generality of His power and the intensity of His might, creates creation ex nihilo without any prior material; and by the greatness of His subtle kindness and the perfection of His wisdom, He creates one thing from another, not out of need, for He is holy (quddus) above needs and free from defects (salam), as He said: "the Holy, the Peace." So He created Adam from the earth, created Eve from Adam, and created offspring from both of them, arranged upon intercourse, existing as a result of conception, present in the foetus through delivery. As the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the man's water precedes the woman's water, the child is male; and when the woman's water precedes the man's water, the child is female" [[It is narrated with the alif (a long vowel) and light nun, and also with the short vowel and doubled nun.]]. Likewise in the Sahih as well: "When the man's water prevails over the woman's water, the child resembles his paternal uncles; and when the woman's water prevails over the man's water, the child resembles his maternal uncles."

I say: this is the meaning of the hadith of 'A'isha, not its wording. Muslim transmitted it from the narration of 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr from her: a woman said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Does a woman perform ghusl if she has a wet dream and sees the fluid?" He said: "Yes." 'A'isha said to her: "May your hands be dusted and may you be ..." [[The phrase "tariat yadaka" means: may you not succeed! Originally it means that dust has come onto your hand, and that you did not attain any good, i.e., you became poor. But they do not intend by it a curse upon the one addressed, as they say: "May Allah fight him," and so on. The phrase "wa allat" means she cried out because of the severity of this statement. It is also narrated with a damma on the hamza and doubled lam, meaning she was pierced by the arguments, which is a spear. Ibn al-Athir said: this is far-fetched, because it does not suit the wording of the hadith.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let her be. Does resemblance come from anything other than that? When the woman's fluid prevails over the man's fluid, the child resembles his maternal uncles; and when the man's fluid prevails over hers, the child resembles his paternal uncles."

Our scholars said: according to the requirement of this hadith, prevalence necessitates resemblance. It has also come in the hadith of Thawban, which Muslim also transmitted, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the Jew: "The man's water is white and the woman's water is yellow. When the two combine, if the man's semen prevails over the woman's semen, it is male by the permission of Allah; and if the woman's semen prevails over the man's semen, it is female by the permission of Allah..."

...(the hadith). He also made, in this hadith, the "uluw" (here, precedence or superiority) entail maleness and femaleness. Thus, according to the two hadiths, it would follow that if the man's water prevails, the child resembles his paternal uncles and is male, and likewise, if the woman's water prevails, the child resembles its maternal uncles and is female, because the two are effects of one cause. But the matter is not so. Rather, what is observed is contrary to this, for we find children resembling their maternal uncles and being male, and resembling their paternal uncles and being female. Therefore, one of the two hadiths must be interpreted. The one that must be interpreted is the hadith of Thawban. It is said: that "uluw" means that the water reached the womb first. Its basis is that "uluw," when its meaning is domination, comes from their saying: "So-and-so outran me (sabaqani), so I outran him (sabaqtuhu)," meaning I overcame him. From this is the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿And We are not to be outrun﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 60], meaning, not overcome. It was said [in the sense of] "he overcame him," "he prevailed." This interpretation is supported by his saying in the hadith: "If the man's water precedes the woman's water, the child is male, and if the woman's water precedes the man's water, the child is female."

Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi built upon these hadiths a structure. He said: The two waters have four states: First, the man's water comes out first. Second, the woman's water comes out first. Third, the man's water comes out first and is more abundant. Fourth, the woman's water comes out first and is more abundant. The division is completed by the man's water coming out first and then the woman's water coming out after it and being more abundant, or the reverse. So if the man's water comes out first and is more abundant, the child is male by the rule of precedence, and it resembles its paternal uncles by the rule of abundance. If the woman's water comes out first and is more abundant, the child is female by the rule of precedence, and it resembles its maternal uncles by the rule of dominance. If the man's water comes out first, but then the woman's water comes out after it and is more abundant, the child is male by the rule of precedence and resembles its maternal uncles by the rule of the dominance of the woman's water. If the woman's water comes out first, but then the man's water comes out and is higher than the woman's water, the child is female by the rule of the precedence of the woman's water, and resembles its paternal uncles by the rule of the dominance of the man's water. He said: By arranging these divisions, the discourse is set in order, the contradiction among the hadiths is removed, so glory be to the Creator, the All-Knowing.

The third matter: Our scholars said: The creation was consistently male and female until, in the first Jahiliyyah, the khuntha (the hermaphrodite, one of indeterminate sex) occurred. He was brought to 'Amir ibn al-Zarib, the chief and the one of the Arabs relied upon (it is said that he lived three hundred years), and he did not know what to say about him, and he deferred them concerning him. When night fell upon him, his place became strange to him, his bed was disturbed for him, and he kept tossing and turning, and thoughts came to him and went, until his servant noticed his condition and said: "What is wrong with you?" He said to her: "I have stayed awake over a matter I intended, and I do not know what to say about it." She said: "What is it?" He said to her: "A man who has a penis and a vulva, what is his status in inheritance?" The maidservant said to him: "Give him an inheritance according to where he urinates." So he understood her and in the morning he presented it to them, and they returned satisfied with it. Islam came upon that, and it did not descend (as a ruling) except in the time of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who judged regarding it.

The faraid scholars narrated, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he was asked about a newborn that has a front passage and a penis: "From where does he inherit?" He said: "From where he urinates." It is also narrated that a khuntha from the Ansar was brought, and he said: "Give him an inheritance from where he first urinates." Likewise Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah narrated from 'Ali, and similar from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn al-Musayyab, Abu Hanifah, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said the same, and al-Muzani related it from al-Shafi'i. Some people said: There is no indication in urination. If urine comes out from both, Abu Yusuf said: The judgment is according to the greater amount. Abu Hanifah rejected this and said: "Are you going to weigh it?" The companions of al-Shafi'i did not assign a ruling to abundance. It is related from 'Ali and al-Hasan that they said: His ribs are counted, for the woman has one rib more than the man. What the scholars said on this has already passed in the verse of inheritance in "an-Nisa'," thoroughly, and praise be to Allah.

The fourth matter: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said: Some of the leading common people denied the existence of the khuntha, because Allah Most High divided creation into male and female. We say: This is ignorance of the language, heedlessness of the eloquence of its structure, and a failure to grasp the breadth of power. As for the power of Allah, glory be to Him, He is Vast and All-Knowing. As for the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, it does not negate the existence of the khuntha, for Allah Most High said: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills﴾. This is a general praise, so it may not be restricted, because power requires it. As for His saying: ﴿He bestows females on whom He wills, and bestows males on whom He wills. Or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes whom He wills barren﴾, this is a report about the general case among existing beings, and it remained silent about mentioning the rare case, because it falls under the generality of the first statement. Existence bears witness to it, and direct observation refutes the one who denies it. With us, at the ribat of Abu Sa'id, in the presence of the martyr imam from the lands of the Maghrib, there was a khuntha who read with us. He had no beard, had two breasts, and had a female slave. Your Lord knows best about him. Despite long companionship, shyness prevented me from asking him, and today I wish I had uncovered his condition.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 51:

There are two issues in this.

The first: His saying, Exalted is He, "It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation" (wahy). The reason for this is that the Jews said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Will you not speak to Allah and look at Him, if you are a prophet, as Musa spoke to Him and looked at Him? For we will not believe in you until you do that." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed Musa will not look at Him." So there was revealed, "It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation." This was mentioned by al-Naqqash, al-Wahidi and al-Tha'labi.

"Wahyan" (revelation): Mujahid said: it is that He breathes (nafatha yanfuthu) into his heart, so it becomes inspiration (ilham). From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed the Holy Spirit breathed into my heart (rawʿ) that no soul will die until it completes its provision and its term. So fear Allah and seek provision graciously. Take what is lawful and leave what is unlawful." [[al-Raw' (with a damma): the heart and the mind. Al-Raw' (with a fatha): fear.]]

"Or from behind a veil" (min wara'i hijab), as He spoke to Musa. "Or sends a messenger" (yursila rasulan), as He sent Jibril, upon him be peace. It has also been said: "except by revelation" means a vision that he sees in his sleep; this was said by Muhammad ibn Zuhayr. "Or from behind a veil," as He spoke to Musa. "Or sends a messenger": Zuhayr said this is Jibril, upon him be peace.

"Then He reveals by His permission what He wills." This revelation from the messengers is an address from them to the prophets, who hear it as speech and see it directly. Such was the condition of Jibril, upon him be peace, when he descended with the revelation to the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn 'Abbas said: Jibril, upon him be peace, descended to every prophet, but of them only Muhammad, 'Isa, Musa and Zakariyya, upon them be peace, saw him. As for others, it was revelation as inspiration in a dream. It has also been said that "except by revelation" refers to sending Jibril, "or from behind a veil" as He spoke to Musa, "or sends a messenger" to people generally.

Al-Zuhri, Shayba and Nafi' read "aw yursila rasulan fa-yuhiya" with both verbs in the nominative (raf'). The rest read them in the accusative (nasb). The nominative is on the basis of resumption (isti'naf), meaning "and He sends." It has also been said that "yursilu" in the nominative is in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal), the implied meaning being "except by inspiring or sending." Whoever reads in the accusative makes them coordinate with the place (mahall) of "wahy," since its meaning is "and it is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except that He reveals or sends." It is also permissible that the accusative is by the deletion of the governing preposition from the hidden "an" (that), and it then occupies the position of a circumstantial clause, the implied meaning being "or by sending a messenger." It is not permissible to coordinate "aw yursila" in the accusative with "an yukallimahu," because the meaning would be corrupted: it would become "it is not for a human that He should send to him, or that He should send a messenger to him," whereas He did send messengers from among humans and sent them to people.

The second issue: Those who hold that, concerning one who swears not to speak to a man and then sends a messenger to him, he has broken his oath (hanith), have cited this verse, because the one sent is called in it a speaker to the one to whom he is sent, unless the swearer intends face-to-face address. Ibn al-Mundhir said: They differed concerning a man who swears not to speak to so-and-so, then writes to him a letter or sends him a messenger. Al-Thawri said: The messenger is not speech. Al-Shafi'i said: He does not break his oath (la yahnath). Al-Nakha'i said: The ruling concerning a letter is that he breaks it. Malik said: He breaks it with both the letter and the messenger. He said at another time: The messenger is easier than the letter. Abu 'Ubayd said: Speech is other than writing and gesture. Abu Thawr said: He does not break it with a letter. Ibn al-Mundhir said: He does not break it with either the letter or the messenger. I say: This is the view of Malik. Abu 'Umar said: Whoever swears not to speak to a man and greets him, intentionally or forgetfully, or greets a group in which he is included, has broken his oath in all of that according to Malik. If he sends a messenger to him, or greets him during prayer, he does not break it. I say: He breaks it with the messenger unless he intends direct speech, because of the verse; this is the view of Malik and Ibn al-Majishun. This meaning has already been treated in full by our scholars at the beginning of "Surat Maryam" [[see vol. 11 p. 86]], and praise be to Allah.

**First matter:** Allah's words, ﴿And thus did We reveal to you﴾. That is, just as We revealed to the prophets before you, We revealed to you **"a spirit" (rūḥan)**, meaning prophethood. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said it means mercy from Us. As-Suddi said it means revelation (waḥy). Al-Kalbi said it means the Book. Ar-Rabiʿ said it is Jibril. Ad-Dahhak said it is the Qur'an, and this is also the view of Malik ibn Dinar. He called it a spirit because in it there is life from the death of ignorance. He made it "from His command," meaning He sent it down as He wills, to whom He wills, in its inimitable arrangement and its wondrous composition. The words "They ask you about the spirit" [Al-Isra: 85] may also be understood as referring to the Qur'an: ﴿Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord﴾ [Al-Isra: 85], that is, they ask you where this Qur'an came from. Say: it is from the command of Allah, which He sent down to me as a miracle. This was mentioned by al-Qushayri. Malik ibn Dinar used to say: "O people of the Qur'an, what has the Qur'an planted in your hearts? For the Qur'an is the spring of the hearts, just as rain is the spring of the earth."

**Second matter:** Allah's words, ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾. That is, you did not know the path to faith. The apparent meaning of this indicates that before the revelation he was not characterised by faith. Al-Qushayri said: "This is one of the things that the intellect may permit (or: one of the wondrous things of reason)." What most scholars have adopted is that Allah sent no prophet except that he was a believer in Him before his mission. But this is a dogmatic claim, unless it is established by a definitive textual proof. The Qadi Abu al-Fadl ʿIyad said: As for their protection from this (i.e., from sin/doubt) before prophethood, people differ on it. The correct view is that they are protected before prophethood from ignorance of Allah and His attributes and from doubt about any of that. The reports and traditions have agreed on the prophets' being free of this deficiency from the time they were born, and their upbringing upon monotheism and faith, indeed upon the radiance of the lights of knowledge and the breezes of the gentle favours of felicity. Whoever examines their biographies from their childhood until their mission will verify this, as is known of the conditions of Musa, ʿIsa, Yahya, Sulayman and others, peace be upon them. Allah said: ﴿And We gave him wisdom as a child﴾ [Maryam: 12]. The exegetes said: Yahya was given knowledge of the Book of Allah in his childhood. Maʿmar said: He was two or three years old, and the children said to him: "Why don't you play?" He said: "Was I created for play?" It was also said regarding Allah's words ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾ [Al ʿImran: 39] that Yahya confirmed ʿIsa when he was three years old, and so he testified that he was the Word of Allah and His Spirit. It was also said that he confirmed him while he was in his mother's womb. Yahya's mother used to say to Maryam: "I find that what is in my belly prostrates to what is in your belly, as a greeting to it." Allah has also stated the words of ʿIsa to his mother at her giving birth to him, in His words ﴿Do not grieve﴾ [Maryam: 24], according to the reading of the one who reads "from beneath her" (min taḥtihā). And according to the view of the one who said the one calling out was ʿIsa, and his speech in the cradle was stated: ﴿I am the servant of Allah; He has given me the Book and made me a prophet﴾ [Maryam: 30]. And He said: ﴿So We gave understanding of it to Sulayman, and to each We gave judgement and knowledge﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 79]. It has been mentioned of Sulayman's judgement while he was a child playing, in the story of the woman to be stoned and in the story of the child, what his father Dawud acted upon. Al-Tabari reported that his age when he was given kingship was twelve years. Likewise the story of Musa with Pharaoh, when he took hold of his beard while he was still a child. The exegetes said regarding Allah's words ﴿And We gave Ibrahim his right judgement before this﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 51]: that is, We guided him when he was young. Mujahid and others said this. Ibn ʿAta said: He chose him before He brought forth his creation. Some of them said: When Ibrahim was born, Allah sent to him an angel commanding him, on Allah's behalf, to know Him in his heart and to mention Him with his tongue. He said: "I have done it," and did not say "I will do it." That was his right judgement. It was also said that Ibrahim's being cast into the fire and his trial took place when he was sixteen years old; that Ishaq's being tested by slaughter was when he was seven years old; and that Ibrahim's reasoning with the star, the moon and the sun happened when he was fifteen years old [in the originals: "fifteen months"; see vol. 7 p. 25]. It was also said that revelation came to Yusuf while he was a child, when his brothers were about to throw him into the well, through Allah's words: ﴿And We revealed to him: you will surely inform them of this matter of theirs﴾ [Yusuf: 15], and so on, among other reports about them. The people of the biographies have related that Aminah bint Wahb was told that our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) was born with his hands spread out upon the earth and his head raised toward the sky. In his own words (ﷺ), he said: "When I grew up, idols were made hateful to me, and poetry was made hateful to me, and I never intended anything of what the Jahiliyyah used to do except twice, and Allah protected me from them, and I did not return to them." Then the matter becomes firmly established for them; the breezes of Allah's favour follow upon them in succession, and the lights of knowledge shine in their hearts, until they reach the utmost limit, and by Allah's choosing them for prophethood they attain the noble qualities to their utmost, without training or discipline. Allah said: ﴿And when he reached his maturity and was firmly established, We gave him judgement and knowledge﴾ [Al-Qasas: 14] [cited as Yusuf: 22]. The Qadi said: None of the people of reports has transmitted that anyone was made a prophet and chosen from among those known for disbelief and polytheism before that. The basis of this chapter is transmission. Some have argued that hearts recoil from one whose course was of this kind.

The Qadi said: I say that Quraysh hurled at our Prophet, peace be upon him, everything they invented, and the disbelievers of the nations reproached their prophets with everything they could and fabricated, whether what Allah stated or what the transmitters conveyed to us. And we do not find, in any of that, a reproach to any one of them for abandoning their gods, or a rebuke blaming him for leaving what they had gathered upon. Had this been so, they would have hastened to it and used it against him concerning his god. Their reproach to him for forbidding them what they had worshipped before would have been more grievous and more decisive in argument than their reproach to him for forbidding them to leave their gods and what their forefathers had worshipped before. So their unanimous turning away from him is evidence that they did not find a way to it, for had it been transmitted they would not have kept silent about it, just as they did not keep silent about the change of the qibla, and they said ﴿What has turned them away from their qiblah which they used to face?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 142], as Allah related of them.

**Third matter:** The scholars have discussed our Prophet (ﷺ): whether he was worshipping according to a religion before the revelation or not. Some of them rejected that absolutely and deemed it impossible by reason. They said: it is unlikely that one who was known as a follower should be one who is followed. They built this on the doctrine of good and evil (by reason). Another group held a stance of suspension regarding his case, refraining from passing a definitive ruling on it, since reason does not make either of the two possibilities necessary and clear transmission did not establish either of them; this is the view of Abu al-Maʿali. A third group said: he was worshipping according to the law of those before him and acting upon it. Then these differed on the specifics. One group said he was upon the religion of ʿIsa, since it abrogates all religions and creeds before it, so it is not permissible for the Prophet to be upon an abrogated religion. Another group said he was upon the religion of Ibrahim, because he was of his descendants, and he is the father of the prophets. Another group said he was upon the religion of Musa, because it is the oldest of the religions. The Muʿtazila (a theological school) held that he must have been upon some religion, but the specific religion is not known to us. Our leading scholars have refuted all these views, since they are conflicting statements with no decisive proof, although reason permits all of them. What is affirmed with certainty is that he, peace be upon him, was not attributed to any one of the prophets in a manner that would require him to be one of their community and addressed by their entire law. Rather, his law is independent in itself, originating from the Almighty, the Wise, may He be exalted. He (ﷺ) was a believer in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; he never prostrated to an idol, never associated anything with Allah, never committed adultery, never drank wine, never attended the sammar (the place where people gather for evening conversation), never attended the Hilf al-Mutayyibin (the alliance of the Perfumed) or the Hilf al-Muṭayyab (in the originals: "al-Muṭayyab"; Ibn al-Athir said: "The origin of a ḥilf is a covenant and pact for mutual support, aid and agreement. What was in the Jahiliyyah for strife, fighting between tribes and raids, is what the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade in Islam when he said: 'There is no ḥilf in Islam.' What was in the Jahiliyyah for supporting the oppressed and maintaining the ties of kinship, like the Ḥilf al-Mutayyibin and what took its course, is what the Messenger (ﷺ) spoke of when he said: 'Any ḥilf that was in the Jahiliyyah, Islam only increased it in strength.' He means a covenant for good and for supporting the truth. By this the two ḥadiths are reconciled, and this is the ḥilf that Islam requires. The Banu Hashim, Banu Zuhrah and Taym gathered in the house of Ibn Jadʿan in the Jahiliyyah, put perfume in a bowl, dipped their hands in it, and made a pact to support one another and to take from the oppressor on behalf of the oppressed; hence they were called "the Perfumed." He (ﷺ) also said: "I witnessed in the house of ʿAbdullah ibn Jadʿan a ḥilf such that, if I were invited to its like in Islam, I would answer." Ibn al-Athir said: he means the Ḥilf al-Fuḍul (the Alliance of the Virtuous).

(See Ibn al-Athir's *al-Nihaya*, entry *ḥalafa*. *Ṭayyib*. *Faḍl*.) Rather, Allah has declared him free from that and protected him from it.

If it is said: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shayba narrated a hadith with his chain from Jabir that the Prophet ﷺ used to attend the gatherings of the polytheists, and he heard two angels behind him, one of whom said to his companion: "Go until you stand behind him." The other said: "How can I stand behind him when his covenant was to touch the idols, and he has not yet attended them?"' The answer is that this is a hadith which Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal denounced strongly, saying: "This is fabricated, or close to fabricated." Al-Daraqutni said: "'Uthman erred in its chain. The hadith as a whole is munkar (rejected) and its chain is not agreed upon, so it should not be considered. What is known from the Prophet ﷺ, according to the scholars, is the opposite of it: his saying, 'The idols were made hateful to me,' and his words in the story of Bahira, when he made the Prophet ﷺ swear by al-Lat and al-Uzza when he met him in Syria on a journey with his uncle Abu Talib, while he was a boy. Bahira had seen in him the signs of prophethood and tested him with this. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'Do not ask me by them, for by Allah I have never hated anything as much as I hate them.' Bahira said to him: 'Then by Allah, tell me what I ask you about.' He said: 'Ask what you wish.'" Likewise, what is known of his biography, peace be upon him, and of Allah's granting him success, is that before his prophethood he differed from the polytheists in their standing at Muzdalifa during the Hajj, and he would stand at 'Arafat, because it was the standing place of Ibrahim, peace be upon him.

If it is said: Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Say: Rather, the religion of Ibrahim﴾ [al-Baqarah: 135], and He said: ﴿Then We revealed to you: follow the religion of Ibrahim﴾ [al-Nahl: 123, 12 in the numbering given], and He said: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion﴾ [al-Shura: 13], and so on. This implies that he was worshipping according to a sacred law. The answer is that this refers to what the sacred laws do not differ on, namely monotheism and establishing the religion, as has been explained previously in more than one place, and in this surah at His saying ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion﴾ [al-Shura: 13]. And praise be to Allah.

Fourth: Having established this, know that the scholars differed in interpreting the Exalted's saying: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾. A group said: the meaning of "faith" (*īmān*) in this verse is the sacred laws of faith and its markers, related by al-Tha'labi. It was also said: the details of this sacred law, meaning you were unaware of these details. It is permissible to apply the word "faith" to the details of the law, related by al-Qushayri. It was also said: you did not know before the revelation that you would recite the Qur'an, nor how to call people to faith, and similar was reported from Abu al-'Aliya. Bakr al-Qadi said: nor the faith which consists of the obligations and rulings. He said: Before this he was a believer in His oneness, then the obligations came down which he did not know before, so he increased in faith through the obligation. These four views are close to one another. Ibn Khuzayma said: by "faith" is meant the prayer, based on the Exalted's saying: ﴿Allah would not let your faith be lost﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143], meaning your prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis. So the word is general but the intended meaning is specific. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: meaning, you did not know what the Book was, nor the people of faith. This is an instance of omitting the modified noun, i.e., who is the one who believes? Abu Talib, or al-'Abbas, or others. It was also said: you did not know anything when you were in the cradle and before puberty. al-Mawardi related something similar from 'Ali ibn 'Isa, who said: You did not know what the Book was, were it not for the message, nor faith, were it not for puberty. It was also said: You did not know what the Book was were it not for Our favour upon you, nor faith were it not for Our guidance of you, and this is possible. Regarding this "faith" there are two aspects: the first is that it is faith in Allah, and he knew this after his puberty and before his prophethood. The second is that it is the religion of Islam, and he did not know this except after prophethood.

I say: He ﷺ was a believer in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from the time he grew up until the time he reached puberty, as has been mentioned before. It was also said: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾ means: you were of an unlettered people who did not know the Book or faith, so that you could have taken what you brought them from someone among them who knew that. This is like the Exalted's saying: ﴿You did not recite before it any book, nor did you write it with your right hand, for then the falsifiers would have doubted﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 48]. This meaning was related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. ﴿But We made it﴾: Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak said: meaning faith. al-Suddi said: the Qur'an. It was also said: the revelation, meaning We made this revelation ﴿a light by which We guide whom We will﴾, i.e., whom We choose for prophethood, like the Exalted's saying: ﴿He singles out for His mercy whom He wills﴾ [Al 'Imran: 74]. The pronoun is singular because the act, with the multiplicity of its names, is like the act with a single name. Do you not see that you say: "Your coming and your going please me," using the singular, though they are two? ﴿And indeed you guide﴾, i.e., you call and direct ﴿to a straight path﴾, an upright religion with no crookedness in it. 'Ali said: to a straight book. 'Asim al-Jahdari and Hawshab read ﴿And indeed you are guided﴾ with the passive voice, meaning you are called. The rest read ﴿You guide﴾ with the active voice. In the reading of Ubayy: ﴿And indeed you call﴾. al-Nahhas said: This is not recited, because it contradicts the *sawad* (the consonantal text of the Qur'an), and such readings are only understood as coming from their reporter as an explanation, as with "and indeed you guide", meaning you call. Ma'mar related from Qatada regarding the Exalted's saying ﴿And indeed you guide to a straight path﴾ that he said: ﴿And for every people there is a guide﴾ [al-Ra'd: 7]. [See vol. 9, p. 285.] ﴿The path of Allah﴾ is a substitute for the first, a substitution of a definite for an indefinite. 'Ali said: it is the Qur'an. It was also said: Islam. al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an related it from the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, in ownership, servitude and creation. ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah do all matters return﴾: a warning of resurrection and recompense. Sahl ibn Abi al-Ja'd said: A *mushaf* (copy of the Qur'an) burned and nothing remained but His saying ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah do all matters return﴾, and another *mushaf* drowned and all of it was erased except His saying ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah do all matters return﴾. And praise be to Allah alone.

**First matter:** Allah's words, ﴿And thus did We reveal to you﴾. That is, just as We revealed to the prophets before you, We revealed to you **"a spirit" (rūḥan)**, meaning prophethood. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said it means mercy from Us. As-Suddi said it means revelation (waḥy). Al-Kalbi said it means the Book. Ar-Rabiʿ said it is Jibril. Ad-Dahhak said it is the Qur'an, and this is also the view of Malik ibn Dinar. He called it a spirit because in it there is life from the death of ignorance. He made it "from His command," meaning He sent it down as He wills, to whom He wills, in its inimitable arrangement and its wondrous composition. The words "They ask you about the spirit" [Al-Isra: 85] may also be understood as referring to the Qur'an: ﴿Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord﴾ [Al-Isra: 85], that is, they ask you where this Qur'an came from. Say: it is from the command of Allah, which He sent down to me as a miracle. This was mentioned by al-Qushayri. Malik ibn Dinar used to say: "O people of the Qur'an, what has the Qur'an planted in your hearts? For the Qur'an is the spring of the hearts, just as rain is the spring of the earth."

**Second matter:** Allah's words, ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾. That is, you did not know the path to faith. The apparent meaning of this indicates that before the revelation he was not characterised by faith. Al-Qushayri said: "This is one of the things that the intellect may permit (or: one of the wondrous things of reason)." What most scholars have adopted is that Allah sent no prophet except that he was a believer in Him before his mission. But this is a dogmatic claim, unless it is established by a definitive textual proof. The Qadi Abu al-Fadl ʿIyad said: As for their protection from this (i.e., from sin/doubt) before prophethood, people differ on it. The correct view is that they are protected before prophethood from ignorance of Allah and His attributes and from doubt about any of that. The reports and traditions have agreed on the prophets' being free of this deficiency from the time they were born, and their upbringing upon monotheism and faith, indeed upon the radiance of the lights of knowledge and the breezes of the gentle favours of felicity. Whoever examines their biographies from their childhood until their mission will verify this, as is known of the conditions of Musa, ʿIsa, Yahya, Sulayman and others, peace be upon them. Allah said: ﴿And We gave him wisdom as a child﴾ [Maryam: 12]. The exegetes said: Yahya was given knowledge of the Book of Allah in his childhood. Maʿmar said: He was two or three years old, and the children said to him: "Why don't you play?" He said: "Was I created for play?" It was also said regarding Allah's words ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾ [Al ʿImran: 39] that Yahya confirmed ʿIsa when he was three years old, and so he testified that he was the Word of Allah and His Spirit. It was also said that he confirmed him while he was in his mother's womb. Yahya's mother used to say to Maryam: "I find that what is in my belly prostrates to what is in your belly, as a greeting to it." Allah has also stated the words of ʿIsa to his mother at her giving birth to him, in His words ﴿Do not grieve﴾ [Maryam: 24], according to the reading of the one who reads "from beneath her" (min taḥtihā). And according to the view of the one who said the one calling out was ʿIsa, and his speech in the cradle was stated: ﴿I am the servant of Allah; He has given me the Book and made me a prophet﴾ [Maryam: 30]. And He said: ﴿So We gave understanding of it to Sulayman, and to each We gave judgement and knowledge﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 79]. It has been mentioned of Sulayman's judgement while he was a child playing, in the story of the woman to be stoned and in the story of the child, what his father Dawud acted upon. Al-Tabari reported that his age when he was given kingship was twelve years. Likewise the story of Musa with Pharaoh, when he took hold of his beard while he was still a child. The exegetes said regarding Allah's words ﴿And We gave Ibrahim his right judgement before this﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 51]: that is, We guided him when he was young. Mujahid and others said this. Ibn ʿAta said: He chose him before He brought forth his creation. Some of them said: When Ibrahim was born, Allah sent to him an angel commanding him, on Allah's behalf, to know Him in his heart and to mention Him with his tongue. He said: "I have done it," and did not say "I will do it." That was his right judgement. It was also said that Ibrahim's being cast into the fire and his trial took place when he was sixteen years old; that Ishaq's being tested by slaughter was when he was seven years old; and that Ibrahim's reasoning with the star, the moon and the sun happened when he was fifteen years old [in the originals: "fifteen months"; see vol. 7 p. 25]. It was also said that revelation came to Yusuf while he was a child, when his brothers were about to throw him into the well, through Allah's words: ﴿And We revealed to him: you will surely inform them of this matter of theirs﴾ [Yusuf: 15], and so on, among other reports about them. The people of the biographies have related that Aminah bint Wahb was told that our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) was born with his hands spread out upon the earth and his head raised toward the sky. In his own words (ﷺ), he said: "When I grew up, idols were made hateful to me, and poetry was made hateful to me, and I never intended anything of what the Jahiliyyah used to do except twice, and Allah protected me from them, and I did not return to them." Then the matter becomes firmly established for them; the breezes of Allah's favour follow upon them in succession, and the lights of knowledge shine in their hearts, until they reach the utmost limit, and by Allah's choosing them for prophethood they attain the noble qualities to their utmost, without training or discipline. Allah said: ﴿And when he reached his maturity and was firmly established, We gave him judgement and knowledge﴾ [Al-Qasas: 14] [cited as Yusuf: 22]. The Qadi said: None of the people of reports has transmitted that anyone was made a prophet and chosen from among those known for disbelief and polytheism before that. The basis of this chapter is transmission. Some have argued that hearts recoil from one whose course was of this kind.

The Qadi said: I say that Quraysh hurled at our Prophet, peace be upon him, everything they invented, and the disbelievers of the nations reproached their prophets with everything they could and fabricated, whether what Allah stated or what the transmitters conveyed to us. And we do not find, in any of that, a reproach to any one of them for abandoning their gods, or a rebuke blaming him for leaving what they had gathered upon. Had this been so, they would have hastened to it and used it against him concerning his god. Their reproach to him for forbidding them what they had worshipped before would have been more grievous and more decisive in argument than their reproach to him for forbidding them to leave their gods and what their forefathers had worshipped before. So their unanimous turning away from him is evidence that they did not find a way to it, for had it been transmitted they would not have kept silent about it, just as they did not keep silent about the change of the qibla, and they said ﴿What has turned them away from their qiblah which they used to face?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 142], as Allah related of them.

**Third matter:** The scholars have discussed our Prophet (ﷺ): whether he was worshipping according to a religion before the revelation or not. Some of them rejected that absolutely and deemed it impossible by reason. They said: it is unlikely that one who was known as a follower should be one who is followed. They built this on the doctrine of good and evil (by reason). Another group held a stance of suspension regarding his case, refraining from passing a definitive ruling on it, since reason does not make either of the two possibilities necessary and clear transmission did not establish either of them; this is the view of Abu al-Maʿali. A third group said: he was worshipping according to the law of those before him and acting upon it. Then these differed on the specifics. One group said he was upon the religion of ʿIsa, since it abrogates all religions and creeds before it, so it is not permissible for the Prophet to be upon an abrogated religion. Another group said he was upon the religion of Ibrahim, because he was of his descendants, and he is the father of the prophets. Another group said he was upon the religion of Musa, because it is the oldest of the religions. The Muʿtazila (a theological school) held that he must have been upon some religion, but the specific religion is not known to us. Our leading scholars have refuted all these views, since they are conflicting statements with no decisive proof, although reason permits all of them. What is affirmed with certainty is that he, peace be upon him, was not attributed to any one of the prophets in a manner that would require him to be one of their community and addressed by their entire law. Rather, his law is independent in itself, originating from the Almighty, the Wise, may He be exalted. He (ﷺ) was a believer in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; he never prostrated to an idol, never associated anything with Allah, never committed adultery, never drank wine, never attended the sammar (the place where people gather for evening conversation), never attended the Hilf al-Mutayyibin (the alliance of the Perfumed) or the Hilf al-Muṭayyab (in the originals: "al-Muṭayyab"; Ibn al-Athir said: "The origin of a ḥilf is a covenant and pact for mutual support, aid and agreement. He (ﷺ) also said: "I witnessed in the house of ʿAbdullah ibn Jadʿan a ḥilf such that, if I were invited to its like in Islam, I would answer." Ibn al-Athir said: he means the Ḥilf al-Fuḍul (the Alliance of the Virtuous).

(See Ibn al-Athir's *al-Nihaya*, entry *ḥalafa*. *Ṭayyib*. *Faḍl*.) Rather, Allah has declared him free from that and protected him from it.
